title: In-app toast for non-obvious gameplay events
description:
Replace ephemeral Alert.alert() calls with a non-blocking in-app toast/banner for gameplay events that don't require user interaction.

## Architecture

Drive toasts off the SSE stream (mobile/src/hooks/useGameplayEvents.ts), NOT the push notification payload. Rationale:
- SSE is already delivering every event in real-time while the app is foregrounded.
- iOS/Android suppress push notifications by default while an app is foregrounded, so there's no overlap/dedup concern between the toast and a push banner.
- This is why the 'enable in-app notifications' prompt pattern is unnecessary here — those apps lack a realtime channel and reuse push payloads; we have SSE.

## Toast Component

- **Custom Reanimated banner** (~100 lines) — no new native deps, full control over styling.
- **Top-of-screen**, design-language colors (not system toast styling).
- **Single visible + queue depth 1** — if a second event arrives while one is showing, it waits; no history.
- **5s auto-dismiss**, swipe-to-dismiss, tap-to-dismiss.
- No tap-to-navigate (none of the scoped events require action).

## Rule of Thumb

**Toast when the screen stays. Alert when the screen changes.**
- Events that leave the player on the gameplay screen → toast.
- Events that navigate the player away (self-kick → home, game end → recap) → keep the blocking Alert (or just navigate) since toasts would race screen transitions.
- Events that already open a dedicated UI (FoundClaimModal) → no change.
- Confirmation-style Alerts (veto/abandon/kick/end game/power-up/set-stop) → stay modal — they require user action.

## Events Migrating to Toasts

| Event | Audience | Copy |
|---|---|---|
| `player_left` (other player) | all same-role peers | `"<Name> has left the game"` or `"<Name> was removed by the host"` |
| `host_changed` (new host) | new host only | `"You are the new host"` |
| `host_changed` (others) | all other players | `"<Name> has been made the new host"` |
| `hiding_zone_expanded` | all (including the initiating hider — toast doubles as action feedback) | `"The hiding zone has been expanded to <new radius>"` |
| `proximity_escalated` | hider (channel-gated, already hider-only) | existing strings from `proximityEscalationMessage`, no title |
| `proximity_deescalated` | hider (channel-gated, already hider-only) | existing strings from `proximityDeescalationMessage`, no title |
| `found_claim_rejected` | seeker | `"The hiders rejected your found claim"` |
| `found_claim_expired` | both roles | `"The found claim timed out"` |

New radius for `hiding_zone_expanded`: compute on mobile from `useGameInfo` base radius × 2, formatted per the game's `DistanceConvention` (km / mi).

## Events NOT Changing

- **Self-kick** (`player_left` where `player_id === playerId`): keep the blocking Alert. Screen transitions to home immediately after; a toast would race navigation and be lost.
- **`FoundClaimModal`** (driven by `found_claim` event): already a dedicated pageSheet modal; not an Alert.
- **Confirmation-style Alerts** (veto/abandon/kick/end game/power-up confirms/set-stop confirm): remain modal because they require user decisions.
- **Question lifecycle events** (asked/answered/vetoed/abandoned): already have clear visual affordances (question banner, thermometer, map overlays) — no toast needed.
- **Phase transitions, game_started, game_dissolved, game_ended**: navigation covers these.

## Current State

`mobile/src/hooks/useGameplayEvents.ts` is the only dispatch point to modify. The events above are all currently handled there.

## History

Originally beads-466 (general notification queueing). Narrowed after brainstorming revealed most events already have visual affordances. beads-466 closed as superseded.

title: Seeker question history scrubber with exclusion replay
description:
Add a utility belt entry for seekers that opens a modal with a scrubber/timeline over answered questions.

## Where it lives

mobile/src/components/utility-belt/UtilityBelt.tsx — the seeker utility belt already holds 'Endgame' (opens QuestionCutoffModal). Add the 'History' entry alongside.

## Modal contents

- Standalone mini-map rendering transit lines, stations, and game boundary (independent of the main map — safe to render without affecting main game state).
- At the current scrub position:
  - Cumulative exclusion *through* that point: rendered in red see-through (union of all exclusion deltas from Q1 through current).
  - The scrubbed-to question's *delta* exclusion: rendered in solid question-color, NOT drawn under already-excluded regions. The solid area visually encodes the marginal information value of that specific question — a tiny solid area means the question told us little new; a large area means it narrowed things significantly.
- Question card below scrubber showing type/params/answer at current position (reuse QuestionHistoryRow where appropriate).
- Scrubber is view-only — unlike the endgame cutoff modal, no exclusion setting/cutoff.

## Implementation concern: rendering the delta

'Delta exclusion not drawn under already-excluded regions' is a non-trivial client-side geometry operation (PostGIS ST_Difference equivalent). Candidates:
- @turf/difference — likely already available or easy to add; works on GeoJSON.
- Naive z-ordering (draw cumulative, then draw delta on top) will NOT achieve the effect — colors blend visibly and the cumulative shows through the delta. Must actually subtract geometries before rendering.

## Reference implementation

mobile/src/components/QuestionCutoffModal.tsx already renders a map with exclusion overlays — study its exclusion layer rendering before starting.

## Data source

SeekerQuestionAnsweredEvent carries per-question exclusion geometry; already on client via GameplayStore.question_history. No new endpoints.

## Edge cases

- Empty state: no answered questions yet → show friendly empty message, hide scrubber.
- Single question: scrubber collapses to a single position.
- Scrub to position 0 (before any questions): show boundary + map only, no exclusions.
- Vetoed/abandoned questions: no exclusion geometry — decide whether to include as scrubber stops (likely yes for completeness, but render with no delta overlay).
close_reason: Closed

title: DB-backed timer reconciler to replace Celery ETA for game timers
description:
Game phase transitions (hiding→seeking) and question auto-answers are currently scheduled via Celery's apply_async(countdown=...). This is fragile: Celery's Redis broker hands ETA tasks to a worker immediately, and the worker holds the timer in memory until fire-time. If the worker crashes/restarts/OOMs between scheduling and firing, the timer is lost — with a 180min hiding phase, that's a long uptime requirement for a single request. Redis AOF persistence doesn't help because the task is no longer in Redis.

Fix: stop using Celery ETA. Authoritative fire-times already live in Postgres (Game.hiding_started_at + hiding_time_min, Question.answerable_at). Add a periodic tick (~1s) that queries for overdue rows and enqueues immediate Celery tasks. Celery becomes a worker pool only (what it's good at), never a scheduler. A late restart means timers fire N seconds late, never lost.

Deployment: run Celery Beat as a new docker-compose service alongside api + worker. Beat publishes a 'reconcile_timers' periodic task every 1s; the existing worker picks it up and executes reconciliation using existing Python logic (logic/, broadcast/). Beat is tiny (~50MB, single-purpose), and if it dies for N seconds timers are merely N seconds late.

Rejected alternatives:
- pg_cron inside Postgres — can detect due timers in SQL but can't execute transitions (logic is Python: emit events, clean up locations, send pushes). Would still need a Python consumer, so no simplicity gain.
- Background task inside API server — multiple API replicas would duplicate fires without advisory locks, and API restart cadence would affect timer cadence.
- Inside the Celery worker itself — same SPOF we're trying to escape.

Transitions must be idempotent (double-tick guard — check current status before acting) so a redundant tick after the real one already fired is a no-op.

Call sites to migrate:
- server/src/hideandseek/routers/games.py:332 (transition_hiding_to_seeking)
- server/src/hideandseek/routers/questions.py:82 (auto_answer_question)
close_reason: Implemented in 82631b9: hideandseek-reconciler package polls Postgres every 1s for overdue timers and enqueues existing Celery tasks; routers no longer schedule or revoke.

title: Expose inventory in static game info; clean up question-param denormalization
description:
## Why

Question parameters (radar radius, thermometer min_travel, matching/measuring distance, tentacles category + distance, photo subject) currently flow to mobile clients via the SSE `QuestionAskedEvent.parameters` field, which is then stored mobile-side on the active question. After SSE reconnect, `parameters` is absent from the snapshot, so anything that needs them post-reconnect breaks unless denormalized.

Today's status:
- **Seeker** has `inventory` in `SeekerGameStateResponse` and looks up params via `inventory.find(s => s.slot_index === q.slot_index)`. Works on reconnect. Used by `SeekerBanner.formatQuestionLabel` and `ParamPicker`.
- **Hider** has no inventory. `parameters` is the only source. On reconnect the hider banner falls back to generic strings (or "Photo" for the photo subject).
- **Question history** carries `parameters` per-entry on both `HiderQuestionHistoryEntry` and `SeekerQuestionHistoryEntry`. This is denormalized per-row even though slot_index + game inventory could resolve it.
- **HideAndSeek-z32.7** added `photo_subject` to `HiderActiveQuestion` as a one-off denormalization to dodge this gap. We accepted it as a one-off because photo is the only question type whose hider-side label is parameter-derived. This bead is the proper fix.

Inventory is **static for the lifetime of a game** (`ask_count` increments but the slot's params don't change). The inventory belongs on `GameInfoResponse` (fetched once via `useGameInfo`, `staleTime: Infinity`), not in dynamic SSE state.

## Scope

### Server
- Move (or copy) inventory into `GameInfoResponse`. Either:
  - (a) Promote the existing `InventoryResponse` shape into `GameInfoResponse` and remove it from `SeekerGameStateResponse` (cleanest — but requires mobile to switch the read site).
  - (b) Add it to `GameInfoResponse`, leave it on the seeker dynamic snapshot for one cycle, then remove from dynamic in a follow-up.
  - Pick (a). The seeker's `ask_count` updates flow via `setActiveQuestion` already, so the inventory snapshot doesn't need to live in dynamic state.
- Update `build_game_info()` in `server/src/hideandseek/queries/game_state.py` to populate inventory from `game.inventory_slots`.
- Drop `photo_subject` from `HiderActiveQuestion` (added in z32.7); drop the population in `build_hider_game_state`.
- Consider whether `parameters` should also be removed from `QuestionAskedEvent` — likely keep it for one-shot delta consumers, but confirm nothing else depends on it.
- Question history: drop `parameters` from `HiderQuestionHistoryEntry` and `SeekerQuestionHistoryEntry`; clients resolve via `slot_index` + game info inventory. (Verify: history entries reference slots that still exist on the game, and `ask_count` doesn't matter for historical lookups.)

### Mobile
- `useGameInfo` already provides static info — just consume the new `inventory` field.
- Hider banner can now resolve params for any question type from `gameInfo.inventory`. Update `HiderBanner` to do real param-aware rendering for all types (start with photo subject; consider whether radar/thermometer/etc. should show their distance/min_travel labels too, mirroring seeker).
- `SeekerBanner` switches its inventory read from `useGameplayStore` to `useGameInfo`. Similarly `ParamPicker`, `QuestionTypeBar`, `useQuestionSelection`.
- `SeekerQuestionHistoryModal` / `HiderQuestionHistoryModal` / `QuestionHistoryRow` resolve params from inventory instead of from the entry's `parameters` field.
- Drop the mobile-only `parameters?` extension on `HiderActiveQuestion` / `SeekerActiveQuestion` once everything else is migrated.
- Remove the photo_subject denormalization added in z32.7.

### Tests
- Server: snapshot tests for `GameInfoResponse` carrying inventory; existing inventory tests on the seeker dynamic snapshot get moved/dropped.
- Mobile: tsc + lint clean.

## Why this is P2 not housekeeping

It's user-facing: today the hider banner shows generic "Answer" labels for all question types post-reconnect. With inventory in static info, the hider banner can display the same rich context the seeker has (distance, category, subject) — meaningful UX improvement, not just a refactor.

## Out of scope

- Changing the SSE delta event shapes for non-recovery purposes (e.g. dropping `parameters` from `QuestionAskedEvent` is optional follow-up).
- Tentacles POI list normalization — that one is genuinely dynamic per-ask (POIs depend on seeker location).

title: Separate static game info from dynamic SSE game state

Create a dedicated GET endpoint (e.g. GET /games/{id}/info) for static game info that the client fetches once on game entry and caches. The SSE game_state event then carries only dynamic state, reducing reconnection payload and clarifying data lifecycle. Referenced in design/hider-experience.md §9.

title: Scheduled hider actions: queue veto/randomize before auto-answer deadline
description:
Allow hiders to pre-schedule a powerup action (veto or randomize) in response to a question, so they can take maximum strategic time without risking the auto-answer timer firing before they act.

When a question becomes answerable, the hider has three choices:
1. Answer immediately
2. Wait and answer/play powerup manually before the timer expires
3. Schedule a powerup action — the server holds it and executes it just before the auto-answer would fire

This is important because the hider may want to use the full timer duration strategically (e.g. to move to a better position) but can't risk the auto-answer resolving the question normally.

Key design points:
- New endpoint: POST /questions/{id}/schedule-action with action type (veto/randomize).
- Scheduled action replaces the auto-answer task — if the hider doesn't answer manually before the deadline, the scheduled powerup fires instead of auto-answer.
- Hider can cancel a scheduled action and answer normally instead.
- If hider answers manually before the deadline, the scheduled action is discarded.
- Depends on veto and randomize powerups being implemented first.
close_reason: Scheduled veto implemented via ?scheduled=true on veto endpoint. Auto-answer task checks scheduled_veto flag and vetoes instead of computing answer. Scheduled randomize deferred until randomize powerup (HideAndSeek-fcz) lands.

title: Investigate after-commit emit for worker timer tasks
description:
Worker timer tasks (worker/src/hideandseek_worker/tasks/game_timers.py) currently use emit_gameplay_now() — immediate Redis publish, no transactional gating. The reasoning is that the reconciler retry loop makes leaked events self-healing: if commit rolls back after emit, next reconciler tick re-enqueues the task and clients converge.

Investigate whether we should switch workers to emit_gameplay() (after-commit) too, for consistency and to eliminate the leaked-event-then-retry failure mode entirely. Considerations:
- Workers use session_scope() — does it cleanly integrate with the Session-level after_commit listener? (It should; same SQLAlchemy Session class.)
- Does removing the leaked-event window measurably improve UX, or is the reconciler retry fast enough that users never see the inconsistency?
- Are there worker code paths that intentionally publish before commit (probably not, but worth checking)?
- Cost: rename ~10 call sites back, drop the emit_gameplay_now public API entirely (or keep for future unanticipated cases).

If the answer is yes, this becomes a small follow-up refactor. If no, document the why in core/CLAUDE.md so the question doesn't get re-litigated.

title: Background location updates for mobile
description:
Enable the mobile app to continue reporting player location to the server while the app is backgrounded or the screen is off. Critical for gameplay: hiders and seekers need location tracking to remain active when the phone is in a pocket / screen locked during transit. Without this, the game breaks when players stop actively looking at the screen.

Requirements:
- iOS: background location mode (expo-location background updates)
- Android: foreground service with persistent notification for location tracking
- Respect 10s update interval convention (see feedback_location_update_interval.md)
- Stop background updates when game ends / player leaves
- Handle permission prompts (always-allow on iOS, background on Android)
- Battery-conscious: use significant-change / deferred updates where possible

title: SSE event gap detection via per-game sequence numbers
description: Clients currently only detect missed SSE events on disconnect. If Redis pub/sub drops a message silently (no disconnect), the client stays out of sync until the next reconnect. Add a monotonic per-game sequence number to every SSE event so clients can detect gaps (expected seq+1, got seq+3) and trigger a resync via the existing state-snapshot GET. No need to store event payloads — the snapshot endpoint already exists as the recovery path. Design question: where does the counter live? Options: (a) a single GameEventSeq column atomically incremented per emit, or (b) a full event log table keyed by (game_id, seq) which gives us replay for free. (a) is cheaper; (b) is more powerful. Leverages SSE's native id: field + Last-Event-ID header.

title: Early hiding zone declaration + ambiguous overlap resolution
description:
Design doc: `design/hider-station-election.md`

Hiders can voluntarily elect their station during the hiding phase, or the system assigns one at the hiding-to-seeking transition. Ambiguity (0 or 2+ valid candidates) is handled via a dedicated status on the game, with fallback resolution when auto-answer timers fire.

## Key Decisions (from design doc)
- One station per game (hiders travel as a group)
- Election is permanent — no revocation
- All hiders must be within hiding_zone_radius of the elected stop (not just centroid)
- No timing restriction on election
- StationElectionStatus enum: pending | elected | auto_assigned | ambiguous
- Questions blocked while ambiguous; auto-answer fallback resolves first

## Fallback Resolution Cascade
1. All-hiders-in-radius → tightest fit
2. Any-hider-in-radius → shortest min distance
3. Closest (stop, hider) pair

## Endpoints
- GET /nearby-stations?lat=&lng= — stateless, open to all, includes hiding zone polygons
- POST /hider-station — hider-only, permanent election
- GET /hiding-zone?station_id= — open to all, pure geometry query
- GET /hider-station (existing) — extended with station_election_status

title: Gameplay control area: taller layout + non-scrolling question selection
description:
The gameplay utility belt area is feeling crowded as the question types and inventory grow:

- Photo questions made the param picker pills (radar/thermometer/matching/measuring/tentacles/photo subjects) require horizontal scrolling. Even with short labels for photo subjects, scrolling the picker feels worse than seeing all options at once.
- The two-row layout (question type bar + param picker) only gives the param picker a single line at narrow widths.

Two parts:

1) Make the whole control area (utility belt) taller. The map shrinks slightly. Concrete starting point: the belt center grows from one row to a 2-row layout, and the type-bar / param-picker each get more vertical breathing room.

2) Reconsider the question selection UI. Pills work for radar/thermometer (small fixed inventory). They scale poorly to photo subjects (~10 per game size) and probably tentacles when categories grow. Options to evaluate:
   - Wrapping grid of pills (no scroll, 2-3 rows).
   - Bottom-sheet "picker" modal that opens on type tap, full-list visible.
   - Per-type custom layouts (radar/thermometer keep pills; photo opens a modal).

This is fine to defer — current pills are workable. Reach for this when adding more question types or expanding photo subjects.

Touches: mobile only — `mobile/src/components/utility-belt/UtilityBelt.tsx`, `ParamPicker.tsx`, `QuestionTypeBar.tsx`. No server / OpenAPI changes.

title: Mobile: failed game-start spins forever instead of falling back to lobby
description:
Observed during muo.2 QA: the seeker's mobile client tapped Start Game, the server returned 500, and the UI continued spinning indefinitely instead of surfacing the error and reverting to the lobby state.

Repro:
1. Lobby with at least one hider + seeker.
2. Trigger a server-side failure on POST /games/{id}/start (e.g. broken Celery worker — observed when api could not import hideandseek_worker.celery_config).
3. Tap Start Game on the host client.

Expected: error toast/alert + UI returns to lobby state, ready to retry.
Actual: spinner persists, no recovery affordance.

Fix likely lives where the start-game request is dispatched (probably in the lobby screen or its mutation hook): wire onError to clear the in-flight state and surface the failure. Same pattern probably applies to other one-shot 'transition' requests (end game, hider-station election, expand hiding zone) — worth auditing in the same pass.
close_reason: Routers now buffer SSE emits until session_dependency commits; rollback drops them. Verified live: failure injected after emit() → no leaked SSE, DB stays in lobby; happy path + pause/resume regress green. Commit cf2ad9b.

title: Silent-push wake to mitigate iOS stationary-background staleness
description: Background location tracking uses expo-task-manager with movement + timeInterval triggers. On iOS, timeInterval is ignored in background and JS timers are suspended, so a stationary iOS player stops reporting until they move. Mitigation: server sends a silent push (content-available=1) to any player who hasn't reported in N minutes; the push wakes the app long enough to post a single fresh location. Requires: (1) server-side scheduler that scans for stale players and enqueues push, (2) a quiet push payload variant, (3) iOS-side handler that posts a location on silent-push receipt. Out of scope for HideAndSeek-2z2 (background-location). Only iOS needs this — Android foreground service delivers 60s heartbeats naturally.
close_reason: Accepted as works-fine-as-is. Existing 25m foreground/background distanceInterval fires on arrival events (you can't arrive at a hiding spot without >25m travel), so CLVisit would be more battery-efficient but not more informative. representative_hider_location() already uses the freshest hider for answer previews, so one disconnected player doesn't blind the seeker. Proximity only escalates on fresh seeker posts, so stale seekers just hold the last computed tier. Gray pin after 60s honestly signals staleness — disconnection-vs-stationary ambiguity is a property of the hide-and-seek mechanic, not a defect. Silent-push mitigation would buy limited freshness (Apple throttles to ~2-3/hr per device) at significant complexity cost. title: Migrate all datetime columns to TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
description:
## Problem

Every datetime column in our schema is `TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE` (the SQLAlchemy default for `Mapped[datetime]`). Postgres returns these as **naive** Python datetimes, but throughout the codebase we write **tz-aware** datetimes (`datetime.now(UTC)`). The convention "everything is UTC" is enforced only by code reviewer vigilance — the type system doesn't help.

This bites the game-timer pause primitive (`core/src/hideandseek_core/logic/pause.py`) immediately: `resume_game()` does `now - paused_at`, which raises `TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes` the moment `paused_at` is read back from the DB on a subsequent request. The primitive has no production call sites yet (m8r.8 / m8r.nah will wire it up), so the bug is latent — but it WILL crash the first host-pause endpoint that ships.

Surfaced by the test work in HideAndSeek-m8r.7 (`server/tests/test_pause.py` — 8 deadline-shift tests skipped, awaiting this fix).

## Principled fix

Use `TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE` (`timestamptz`) for every timestamp column. Despite the name, `timestamptz` doesn't store a timezone — it stores a UTC instant: Postgres normalizes input to UTC on write, returns tz-aware UTC datetimes on read. Same storage size, same perf as plain `TIMESTAMP`. This makes "everything is UTC" a property of the schema, not a convention.

## Scope

1. Update `models/src/hideandseek_models/` to use `Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(DateTime(timezone=True), ...)` (or set up a `type_annotation_map` entry on `Base`) for every datetime column. Affected models include at least: `Game` (`created_at`, `hiding_started_at`, `hiding_ends_at`, `seeking_started_at`, `paused_at`, `found_claim_at`, `found_claim_expires_at`), `Player`, `Question` (`asked_at`, `answerable_at`, `deadline_at`, `answered_at`, etc.), `LocationUpdate.timestamp`, `PhotoQuestionParams` (`queued_at`, `submitted_at`, `reviewed_at`), `DeviceToken` registration timestamps.
2. Generate an Alembic migration (`uv run alembic revision --autogenerate -m "use timestamptz for all datetime columns"`). Postgres can change `TIMESTAMP` → `TIMESTAMPTZ` in-place (no rewrite needed when assuming UTC) via `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE TIMESTAMPTZ USING ... AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'`. Verify the autogenerated migration uses this form.
3. Audit any code that does `datetime.utcnow()` (returns naive) and replace with `datetime.now(UTC)` (returns aware).
4. **Un-skip the 8 tests in `server/tests/test_pause.py`** (search for `pytest.mark.skip` referencing this bead).

## Verification

- `cd server && uv run pytest tests/test_pause.py` — all 16 tests should pass.
- `cd server && uv run pytest` — full suite green.
- Manual smoke check in Docker: pause a game, restart the API container, resume it. Should not crash.
close_reason: Migrated all 17 datetime columns to TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE via Base.type_annotation_map + hand-written Alembic migration 7b2cab27f4e5. All 8 previously-skipped pause tests un-skipped and passing. Migration applied successfully against running stack; downgrade also verified. No mobile changes needed (parseUtc already accepts both Z and ±HH:MM).

title: Live Activities: at-a-glance game state on lock screen / Dynamic Island
description:
Surface live game state outside the app via OS-level persistent UI — iOS Live Activities (Dynamic Island + lock screen), and whatever Android-side equivalents exist. Low priority: a polish feature, not blocking.

## Why this fits the game

HideAndSeek is a game you play *while moving through the city*. Players want to glance at their phone without unlocking it to check:
- active question timer (both sides)
- hiding phase countdown (hiders)
- question cooldown / when the next ask is available (seekers)
- "your answer is due in X" prompt (hider with pending question)
- found-claim status (both sides)

These are exactly the "ongoing, time-sensitive, one-per-user" shapes that Live Activities were designed for.

## iOS

Live Activities (iOS 16.1+) are a first-class framework (ActivityKit). Updates can come via push (APNs with `apns-push-type: liveactivity`) or from the app foreground. Lock screen + Dynamic Island presentations.

Implementation implications:
- Requires a Widget Extension target in the native iOS project — Expo has a dev-build path for this via [`expo-apple-targets`](https://github.com/EvanBacon/expo-apple-targets) or the newer first-party support; needs a real look to pick.
- The push path is separate from normal APNs notifications — SNS Mobile Push may or may not support the `liveactivity` push type directly; might need to bypass SNS for this channel.
- Swift/SwiftUI for the widget UI itself — no React in the widget.

## Android

There is no direct equivalent. What does exist, in descending order of standardization:
- **Android 14+ progress-style notifications** — ongoing notifications with `ProgressStyle`, closest general-purpose analog.
- **MediaStyle / CallStyle / custom ongoing notifications** — pre-14 path; ongoing notification with a large custom layout, pinned to the top. Works on all Android versions.
- **Samsung Live Notifications** — Samsung-specific extension for phones running One UI 5+. Not portable.
- **Google rumored Live Updates** — announced direction for Android, not yet broadly shipped as of the cutoff; worth re-checking at implementation time.

A sensible Android strategy is probably: a pinned ongoing notification with a custom expanded layout that mirrors the iOS Live Activity content. Not as pretty as Dynamic Island, but functional on every Android phone.

## Open questions

- **Push channel divergence**: iOS Live Activity push is its own APNs type; Android ongoing notifications are just normal data pushes that the app renders. We probably want a single server-side event ("game state tick") that both platforms consume differently, not two separate push pipelines.
- **Update cadence**: APNs rate-limits Live Activity updates (budget per hour). Timers should render client-side via end-timestamp rather than push-per-second. Only state *transitions* (question asked/answered/vetoed, phase change, found claim) should push.
- **End-of-activity dismissal**: Live Activities have a grace window after the activity ends; needs a tidy "game over" terminal state.
- **Opt-in UX**: Activities are permission-gated on iOS and users can disable them per-app. UI for discovery + re-enabling.
- **Does this replace push notifications, or augment them?** Likely augments — push still needed for people who've backgrounded the app without an active Live Activity.

## Prerequisites before starting

- Push infrastructure must be solid on both platforms first (see HideAndSeek-dcz for the Android audit).
- Mobile team must own a Dynamic Island-capable device for meaningful iOS testing (the lock-screen presentation works on any iOS 16.1+ device; Dynamic Island needs 14 Pro+).
- A design pass on what the compact / expanded / minimal presentations actually show — Dynamic Island has three sizes and each needs content.

## Likely component breakdown (children to file later)

- **Design doc** as the first child — platform-parity question is significant and benefits from sketching before coding.
- iOS widget extension scaffold (Swift), wired through Expo config plugin.
- Server-side: emit live-activity-flavored push events at phase / question transitions; probably a new event broadcast channel.
- APNs Live Activity token registration (separate from the normal device token).
- Android ongoing-notification path with a custom layout that mirrors the iOS content.
- Graceful degradation text for users on older iOS / Android devices.

Deferring this until the game has matured enough that players actually play long sessions and would benefit from glanceable state.

title: Photo S3 cleanup lifecycle
description:
Follow-up to HideAndSeek-z32 (photo questions). The photo design deliberately keeps all S3 objects forever — no lifecycle rules, no dedup, no cleanup. This task covers the eventual cleanup story once bucket cost becomes non-trivial or retention becomes a policy concern.

See design/2026-04-21-photo-questions.md §5.1, §10 ("Photos kept forever"), and §11 for context.

## Likely shape

- **Terminal-game sweeper**: scheduled task (Celery beat or reconciler variant) that finds games in a terminal state older than N days, walks their photo questions, deletes S3 objects + nulls `photo_object_key`.
- **Alternative**: S3 lifecycle rules keyed on object prefix + age. Simpler, but loses game-state awareness (deletes objects even for games still in question-history view).
- **Orphan cleanup**: the upload flow leaves orphans on every replacement (§5.3). Sweeper should pick up any object under `<env>/<game_id>/` not referenced by any `photo_question_params.photo_object_key`.
- **Tombstone column**: optional — add `cleaned_up_at` on `PhotoQuestionParams` so repeated sweeps skip rows already handled.

## Blocking considerations

- Must not delete photos while question history is being viewed. Consider "game terminal + 30d" as the floor.
- Must handle failed deletions (network blip, IAM revoked) without corrupting DB state. Two-phase: soft-null in DB first, then delete from S3 (tolerant of missing objects on rerun).
- Cost threshold — track bucket size periodically to know when this actually matters. Until then, this task is pure future-proofing.

## Dependencies

- Depends on HideAndSeek-z32 completing (nothing to sweep until photos exist).

title: Auto-sync SSE event types via OpenAPI schema injection
description:
## Problem

SSE delta event types are maintained by hand in `mobile/src/types/gameplay.ts` (~200 lines) and can silently drift from the server's event dataclasses in `server/src/hideandseek/broadcast/events.py`. REST endpoint types are already auto-synced via the `FastAPI → openapi.yaml → openapi-typescript → schema.d.ts` pipeline, but SSE events are excluded because the streaming endpoints use `include_in_schema=False` and the delta events are plain dataclasses, not Pydantic models.

The primary goal is syncing the **delta event types** — the incremental SSE messages like `QuestionAskedEvent`, `PhaseChangedEvent`, `PlayerLocationEvent`, etc. The initial state snapshots (`HiderGameStateResponse`, `SeekerGameStateResponse`) are already Pydantic and can be included easily, but the deltas are the harder and more important part.

## Approach: OpenAPI schema injection (no fake endpoints)

Register SSE event schemas directly into the OpenAPI spec by customizing `app.openapi()` in the FastAPI app. This injects schemas into `components/schemas` without creating fake endpoints. Then `openapi-typescript` picks them up automatically, and the existing pre-commit hook (`openapi-regen.sh` → `api-types-regen.sh`) keeps everything in sync.

### Step 1: Convert delta event dataclasses to Pydantic schemas

The delta events in `broadcast/events.py` are currently frozen dataclasses. They need Pydantic schema counterparts to generate JSON Schema for OpenAPI injection.

**Key design decision**: Where do the Pydantic event schemas live? Options:
- `schemas/events.py` (new file, parallel to `schemas/response.py`) — keeps schemas package consistent
- Keep the dataclasses in `broadcast/events.py` as the internal representation, Pydantic schemas are the wire format definition

**Lobby delta events to model** (from `broadcast/events.py`):
- `PlayerJoinedEvent` — game: GameResponse, player: PlayerResponse
- `PlayerUpdatedEvent` — game: GameResponse, player: PlayerResponse
- `PlayerLeftEvent` — game: GameResponse, player_id: UUID
- `HostChangedEvent` — game: GameResponse, new_host_player_id: UUID
- `GameStartedEvent` — game: GameResponse

**Gameplay delta events to model** (role-specific — this is the critical part):
- `PlayerLocationEvent` — game_id, player_id, name, color, role, coordinates (GeoJSON Point), timestamp
- `QuestionAskedEvent` — game_id, question_id, question_type, status, asked_by, slot_index, parameters (RadarEventParams | ThermometerEventParams | FeatureEventParams), seeker_location_start, asked_at, ask_count, sequence
- `QuestionAnswerableEvent` — game_id, question_id, question_type, status, seeker_location_end
- `HiderQuestionAnsweredEvent` — hider-only: includes hider_location, hider feature resolution
- `SeekerQuestionAnsweredEvent` — seeker-only: includes exclusion geometry, total_exclusion, no hider data
- `QuestionVetoedEvent` — game_id, question_id, question_type, slot_index
- `QuestionAbandonedEvent` — game_id, question_id, question_type, slot_index
- `PhaseChangedEvent` — game_id, phase, seeking_started_at, station_election_status, hider_station_id
- `StationElectionEvent` — game_id, station_election_status, hider_station_id (hider channel only)
- `GamePlayerLeftEvent` — game_id, player_id

**Question parameter sub-types** (already have Pydantic versions in `schemas/params.py`):
- `RadarParamsResponse`, `ThermometerParamsResponse`, `FeatureParamsResponse`, `FeatureResolution`
- The event dataclasses use their own `RadarEventParams`/`ThermometerEventParams`/`FeatureEventParams` — these should converge with or reference the existing Pydantic param schemas

**Important**: Follow the project convention of separate event classes for role-specific payloads (per feedback_separate_event_classes.md). `HiderQuestionAnsweredEvent` and `SeekerQuestionAnsweredEvent` must remain distinct types in the generated schema.

### Step 2: Inject schemas into OpenAPI spec

1. **Customize `app.openapi()`** (in `server/src/hideandseek/app.py` or wherever the FastAPI app is created):
   - Call the base `openapi()` to get the existing schema
   - Use `.model_json_schema()` on each Pydantic event schema
   - Inject into `openapi_schema["components"]["schemas"]`
   - Handle `$defs` — Pydantic's `.model_json_schema()` puts nested types in `$defs`; these need to be hoisted into `components/schemas` or resolved inline so `openapi-typescript` generates named types, not anonymous inlined objects

2. **Also register initial state snapshots** (already Pydantic, easy wins):
   - `HiderGameStateResponse`, `SeekerGameStateResponse`
   - `HiderActiveQuestion`, `SeekerActiveQuestion`
   - `HiderQuestionHistoryEntry`, `SeekerQuestionHistoryEntry`
   - `GamePlayer`, `RosterPlayer`, `StopResponse`, `InventorySlotResponse`

3. **Consider a discriminated union schema** for each channel's event set:
   - `LobbySSEEvent = PlayerJoinedEvent | PlayerUpdatedEvent | ...` with discriminator on event type
   - `HiderSSEEvent = PlayerLocationEvent | QuestionAskedEvent | HiderQuestionAnsweredEvent | ...`
   - `SeekerSSEEvent = PlayerLocationEvent | QuestionAskedEvent | SeekerQuestionAnsweredEvent | ...`
   - This gives the mobile side a single union type to parse against per channel

### Step 3: Update mobile to use generated types

4. **Replace hand-written types** in `mobile/src/types/gameplay.ts` with imports from `@/api/schema.d.ts`
   - Generated types will be under `components["schemas"]["EventName"]` etc.
   - May want a thin re-export file for ergonomic imports

5. **Update consumers**:
   - `useGameplayEvents.ts` — event parsing and store hydration
   - `useLobbyEvents.ts` — event parsing and cache updates
   - `GameplayStore` and any components importing from `gameplay.ts`

### Validation

6. Diff generated types against current hand-written `gameplay.ts` to catch any existing drift
7. Run mobile typecheck (`npx tsc --noEmit`) to verify all consumers compile
8. Manual test: connect to SSE endpoints, verify events parse correctly with generated types

## Files involved

- `server/src/hideandseek/broadcast/events.py` — existing event dataclasses (internal representation, stays)
- `server/src/hideandseek/schemas/events.py` — **new**: Pydantic schemas for SSE events (wire format)
- `server/src/hideandseek/schemas/response.py` — existing response schemas (also to be registered)
- `server/src/hideandseek/schemas/params.py` — existing question parameter schemas
- `server/src/hideandseek/app.py` — OpenAPI customization hook
- `server/scripts/generate_openapi.py` — verify it picks up custom schemas
- `mobile/src/types/gameplay.ts` — to be replaced by generated types
- `mobile/src/hooks/useGameplayEvents.ts` — update imports
- `mobile/src/hooks/useLobbyEvents.ts` — update imports
- `openapi/openapi.yaml` — will gain SSE event component schemas
- `mobile/src/api/schema.d.ts` — will gain SSE types automatically
close_reason: Implemented: gameplay event dataclasses → Pydantic, OpenAPI schema injection with auto-registration, mobile types auto-generated from spec

title: Opportunistic location updates on API actions
description:
Many API actions are made by players whose current location is known to the client. Rather than relying solely on the dedicated POST /games/{game_id}/location endpoint, we should accept an optional location field on relevant requests and treat it as an implicit location update.

Candidate endpoints:
- POST /games/{game_id}/questions (seeker asking a question — already needs seeker location)
- POST /games/{game_id}/questions/{id}/lock-in (seeker locking in thermometer — uses latest location)
- POST /games/{game_id}/questions/{id}/answer (hider answering — snapshots hider location)

Benefits:
- Reduces location staleness for critical game actions
- Fewer dedicated location report round-trips needed
- More accurate question answers since location is fresh at the moment of action

Implementation:

title: Extract database models into top-level package for migration support
description:
## Motivation

The server's SQLAlchemy models currently live at `server/src/hideandseek/models/`. When we add Alembic migrations, the migration environment needs to import the model metadata — but it shouldn't need the full server package (FastAPI, Celery, push infra, etc.). Extracting models into a standalone top-level package enables:

1. **Clean migration setup** — Alembic imports only the models package, not the server
2. **Dependency isolation** — models package has minimal deps (SQLAlchemy, GeoAlchemy2, shapely, pyproj, pydantic)
3. **Future reuse** — other tools (data scripts, admin CLI) can depend on models without pulling in the server

## Design

Create a new top-level package (e.g. `models/` or `db/`) with its own `pyproject.toml`. The server references it via UV workspace local dependency (`hideandseek-models = { path = '../models' }`).

### What moves
- `models/base.py` — DeclarativeBase
- `models/types.py` — enums, constants, DistrictClass
- `models/geo_types.py` — custom SQLAlchemy column types (ShapelyGeography, ShapelyGeometry)
- All table model files (game, player, question, transit, etc.)
- `models/__init__.py` — re-exports

### What stays in server
- `db.py` (engine, session management, ContextVar plumbing)
- `queries/` (session-dependent DB access)
- Everything else (routers, logic, schemas, etc.)

### Key decisions
- Package name: TBD (e.g. `hideandseek-models`, `hideandseek-db`)
- The models package should have zero dependency on FastAPI or any server infra
- Import paths change from `hideandseek.models` to the new package name — requires updating all imports across server code
- UV workspace configuration needed at monorepo root

### Dependencies for the new package
- sqlalchemy
- geoalchemy2
- shapely
- pyproj (used by geo_types)
- pydantic (DistrictClass in types.py is a BaseModel)

### Blockers / considerations
- Ensure `Base.metadata` is still discoverable by `create_all()` in server startup
- Test fixtures reference models heavily — imports need updating
- OpenAPI generation script imports models — needs updating
- GTFS/seed scripts import models — needs updating
close_reason: Models extracted to top-level hideandseek-models package with UV workspace. All 271 tests passing, Docker build verified, seed scripts verified.

title: Re-askable questions with escalating cost multiplier
description:
Questions can be asked more than once. Each subsequent ask of the same question costs more — 2x on second ask, 3x on third, etc. This is foundational to the veto and randomize powerups (a vetoed question can be re-asked at multiplied cost, and a randomized original question can be re-asked at its original cost).

Current behavior: asking a question consumes the inventory slot (radar/thermometer) or category usage (matching/measuring) permanently. A consumed slot cannot be reused.

New behavior:
- Slot-based (radar/thermometer): a consumed slot can be re-asked. The cost multiplier determines how many "draws" the hider gets (game mechanic, not server-enforced). The slot's consumed_at is set on first ask; re-asks don't change it.
- Category-based (matching/measuring): a used category can be re-asked. Same multiplier logic.
- Track ask count per (game, question identity) to compute the multiplier. Question identity = slot_index for slot-based, (category, feature_class, question_type) for category-based.
- The "one unanswered question at a time" rule still applies — can't re-ask while the previous instance is pending.
- Vetoed questions reset to re-askable at the current multiplier. Randomized originals reset to re-askable at 1x (original cost).

Open questions:
- Should the multiplier be returned in the ask response so the client can display it?
- How to model ask count — new column on InventorySlot/CategoryUsage, or a separate counter?
- Does the server enforce the cost (e.g. block re-ask if hider hasn't drawn enough cards), or is it trust-based like powerups?
close_reason: Unified InventorySlot model, re-askable slots with ask_count, custom slots, fixed measuring exclusion inversion

Geometry handling:
- Points: no pre-computation needed (exact Voronoi at runtime)
- LineStrings: dense sampling along the line, Voronoi of samples, merge cells by parent feature
- Polygons: matching uses containment (ST_Contains) — no Voronoi needed. For measuring/tentacles, reduce to boundary (LineString) then sample.

Pre-computation avoids runtime approximation errors at Voronoi cell boundaries, which could produce incorrect game answers. Store pre-computed cells as Polygon geometries linked to each feature.

title: Hider initial location not shown for up to 30s after hiding phase starts
description:
When the game transitions from lobby to hiding phase, the hider’s pin may be missing on the map for up to 30 seconds — the time until the first location POST fires.

## Why

Foreground tracking in `mobile/src/hooks/useLocationTracking.ts` uses `watchPositionAsync({ distanceInterval: 25 })` plus a trailing 30 s heartbeat. If the hider stays stationary after the hiding phase begins (common — they’re about to pick a transit stop and not moving yet), neither trigger fires:
- The watcher callback does not fire because the hider hasn’t moved 25 m.
- The 30 s heartbeat only schedules after the first successful POST, so it doesn’t fire for the first 30 s either.

Result: the server has no location for the hider, so seekers (and the hider themselves) see no pin until either the hider moves 25 m or 30 s elapses from the first watcher fix.

## Repro

1. Join a game with a hider account, sit on the gameplay screen through the hiding transition.
2. Observe the map: no self-pin for the hider, no hider location on seeker devices.
3. Wait 30 s without moving → pin appears once the heartbeat fires.

## Proposed fix

On the hiding-phase transition (or on gameplay-screen mount when already in hiding), fire a one-time `Location.getCurrentPositionAsync` + POST so the server and all clients see the hider immediately. Then let `watchPositionAsync` + heartbeat continue as normal.

Relevant files:
- `mobile/src/hooks/useLocationTracking.ts` — add explicit initial ping
- `mobile/src/hooks/useGameplayEvents.ts` — handles the `phase_changed` SSE if we want to tie it to the transition

## Scope

Hider-only (seekers don’t POST during hiding). Once fixed, the same pattern should also cover the hiding→seeking transition for seekers, whose location currently comes online the same way.
close_reason: Fixed by firing a one-shot getCurrentPositionAsync when the post-eligibility gate (canPost()) flips false->true. Covers hider at lobby->hiding and seeker at hiding->seeking. Verified in iOS simulator: both pins appear instantly instead of up to 30s.

title: Randomize powerup: hider forces a random replacement question
description:
Hider plays a randomize powerup in response to any answerable question. Instead of answering, the server:
1. Notifies seekers that a randomize was played.
2. Seekers must choose (randomly — dice/RNG) a different unasked question from the same category. For slot-based questions (radar/thermometer), this means a different slot. For category-based (matching/measuring), this means a different category.
3. The randomly chosen replacement question is automatically asked, and the hider answers it normally.
4. The original question is NOT considered asked — it can be re-asked later at its original cost.

Key design points:
- Trust-based: no card/hand tracking. Hider assumed to have the powerup.
- The replacement must be from the same category but different parameters (e.g. 10mi radar → 50mi radar).
- If the replacement resolves to a null answer, that's valid (tough luck).
- The original slot/category is restored (not consumed).
- Auto-answer timer on the original question is revoked; a new timer starts on the replacement.
- Push flow: hider plays randomize → push to seekers → seekers pick random replacement → replacement is asked → hider answers.

Open questions:
- Should the server enforce randomness of the replacement, or trust the seekers to pick randomly?

title: Redact player secret from access logs
description:
AccessLogMiddleware logs all request headers with only `authorization` and `cookie` redacted
(server/src/hideandseek/middleware.py:14 — REDACTED_HEADERS). The `X-Player-Secret` header
is attached to nearly every authenticated request (games, location, questions, endgame, SSE
auth in routers/events.py) and therefore appears in plaintext on every `hideandseek.access`
"request" log line in the `headers` field. In `development`/`production` JSON mode that means
the secret lands in whatever log sink we ship logs to.

Reporter also observed the secret "in responses" — the only authorized place it's returned is
JoinGameResponse.player_secret (schemas/response.py:242), which is the one-shot credential hand-off.
The middleware doesn't log response bodies (only response_size), so if there's a second leak
vector beyond the headers dict, we need to identify it. Candidates to audit while we're in
there:
  - request_body capture in middleware.py:87-91 (POST /games and /games/join bodies don't carry
    the secret — safe — but any future endpoint that accepts the secret in the body would leak)
  - any structlog `bind_contextvars` or `.info(..., player_secret=...)` calls (grep came back clean)
  - error handlers or 4xx responses that might echo headers

Fix:
  1. Add `x-player-secret` to REDACTED_HEADERS in middleware.py (and consider `x-player-id`
     too — it's not secret per se, but it's sensitive PII when combined with the secret).
  2. Grep for any other log calls that might include the raw secret and redact them.
  3. Optional hardening: make REDACTED_HEADERS a substring/regex match so future `x-*-secret`
     or `x-*-token` headers are redacted by default.

Files:
  - server/src/hideandseek/middleware.py (REDACTED_HEADERS set, _parse_headers)
  - server/src/hideandseek/dependencies.py, routers/events.py (where the header is read —
    no logging there today, just confirming)
  - tests: add a case that asserts the access log does not contain the raw secret
close_reason: Fixed in bb47e60: added x-player-secret to REDACTED_HEADERS in AccessLogMiddleware. Response bodies are not logged (middleware tracks response_size only), so that vector was a non-issue.

title: Name CloudWatch log groups explicitly in CDK
description:
Set `logGroupName` on the three `logs.LogGroup` constructs in `infra/cdk/lib/app-stack.ts` (ServerLogGroup, WorkerLogGroup, ReconcilerLogGroup) so they land at stable, human-readable paths like `/hideandseek/server`, `/hideandseek/worker`, `/hideandseek/reconciler` instead of CDK's auto-generated `HideAndSeek-App-ServerLogGroupXXXXXXX-<hash>` names.

## Why

- Easier to find in the console (predictable path, alphabetical grouping).
- CLI + `logs tail` commands become memorable (`aws logs tail /hideandseek/server --follow`) instead of requiring a describe-log-groups first.
- Log insights queries and dashboards can be written against stable names without re-pinning every stack rebuild.
- Cross-account / cross-env comparison is cleaner when names don't carry a per-stack hash.

## Caveat — this is a replacement, not a rename

CloudFormation treats `logGroupName` as a create-time-immutable property. Changing it on an existing stack will **destroy the current log groups and create new ones**, losing any retained log history. Since `removalPolicy: DESTROY` is already set and the retention is `ONE_MONTH`, the actual risk is low — but worth doing either before prod has interesting logs to keep, or with an explicit "we accept losing current logs" go-ahead.

## Implementation

In `infra/cdk/lib/app-stack.ts`, add `logGroupName` to each of the three existing `new logs.LogGroup(...)` calls:

```ts
const serverLogGroup = new logs.LogGroup(this, 'ServerLogGroup', {
  logGroupName: '/hideandseek/server',
  retention: logs.RetentionDays.ONE_MONTH,
  removalPolicy: cdk.RemovalPolicy.DESTROY,
});
// same shape for /hideandseek/worker and /hideandseek/reconciler
```

Verify via `npx cdk diff HideAndSeek-App` before any deploy; confirm with the user before running `cdk deploy`.

## CLAUDE.md update

Note the log group naming convention in `infra/cdk/CLAUDE.md` under AppStack so future log groups (e.g. CloudFront access logs in wos.9) follow the same `/hideandseek/<service>` pattern.

title: Game-timer pause mechanic
description:
General-purpose pause mechanic for the seeking-phase game clock. When engaged, the phase timer and any question-level countdowns that reference it stop advancing until the pause is released.

## Motivation

Several planned features need to freeze time without ending the phase:
- Photo questions (HideAndSeek-z32): prevent hiders from burning the seeking clock with bad-photo spam. While a photo question is under review, the clock should pause.
- Possibly future mechanics: curses, on-foot challenges, negotiated recesses.

No existing mechanic models "time stopped" — `Game.phase_started_at` + elapsed math is naively wall-clock based.

## Surface

- **Data model**: `Game.paused_at: datetime | None` plus `Game.accumulated_pause_duration: Interval` (or equivalent seconds column). When `paused_at` is set, the phase is paused; on release, add `now - paused_at` to `accumulated_pause_duration`.
- **Derived time**: replace raw `now - phase_started_at` calls with a helper `elapsed_in_phase(game)` that subtracts pauses. All timer math (question deadlines, phase transitions, reconciler queries) goes through this helper.
- **Reconciler**: overdue-query time math uses the new helper. Reconciler does NOT poll for "scheduled unpause" events — pause/unpause are explicit triggers.
- **Triggers**: pure infrastructure, no default trigger. Features opt in by calling `pause_game(game, reason)` / `resume_game(game)` from their logic paths. `reason: PauseReason` enum for observability.
- **Events**: `GamePausedEvent` / `GameResumedEvent` on both channels. Mobile shows a visual indicator (dimmed timer, banner "paused — waiting for X").
- **Concurrency**: a single pause counter, reference-counted per reason. Multiple concurrent pause reasons extend the pause until all release.

## Out of scope

- Per-player freezing (that's a different mechanic — the endgame hider freeze is self-contained)
- Pausing during hiding phase (hiding is a fixed countdown, no need)
- UI controls to manually pause (this is infra, not a host tool)

## Children (file after this epic is scoped)

- models + Alembic (`Game.paused_at`, `Game.accumulated_pause_duration`, `PauseReason` enum)
- core: `pause_game` / `resume_game` logic, `elapsed_in_phase` helper, event schemas
- reconciler: overdue-query math goes through the helper
- mobile: paused-state visual treatment on belt timer + any question banners
- tests: pause/resume + multi-reason accounting + reconciler interaction
design:
## Design decision (2026-04-25): future-deadline anchors + pause primitive

The original sketch used start-anchor columns (`Game.paused_at` + `accumulated_pause_duration`) and computed deadlines as `start + duration ± pause`. Two problems pushed us to reframe:

1. A single game-wide accumulator misattributes pauses that pre-existed a timer's creation. Per-row offset snapshots fix it but spread pause-awareness across the schema.
2. Mutating `seeking_started_at` / `answerable_at` (the obvious "shift the anchor" alternative) makes column names lie — a `*_started_at` that has been moved forward to compensate for pauses no longer means what its name says.

### The reframe

For every clock the reconciler actually fires, store a future-dated deadline column instead of a past-dated start anchor. While the deadline is in the future, mutating it is honest (we haven't promised it'd fire then). Once it elapses or its row terminates, it freezes.

| Today (start anchor + duration) | Reframed (future deadline) |
|---|---|
| `Game.hiding_started_at` + `hiding_time_min` | `Game.hiding_ends_at` |
| `Question.answerable_at` + `base_question_delay_min` | `Question.deadline_at` |
| `Game.found_claim_at` + `120s` | `Game.found_claim_expires_at` |
| (z32.5) `submitted_at` + `photo_review_sec` | `PhotoQuestionParams.review_deadline_at` |
| (z32.5) `answerable_at` + `photo_submit_min` | `PhotoQuestionParams.submit_deadline_at` |

Existing `*_started_at` / `*_at` columns stay as immutable audit timestamps — they just stop being read for deadline math. `validators.py`'s "is a claim active?" check becomes `found_claim_expires_at IS NOT NULL` (same semantics, the new field name now encodes "live future event").

Durations on the game (`hiding_time_min`, `base_question_delay_min`, `photo_*_min`) stay as configured-value metadata — they're what we use to stamp the deadline at creation, plus display ("the hiding phase is 60 minutes").

### Pause primitive

- `Game.paused_at: datetime | None` — non-null while paused.
- `Game.active_pause_reasons: list[PauseReason]` (JSON) — idempotent set; pause = add reason, resume = remove. Empty ↔ non-empty transitions are the freeze/thaw moments. Multi-reason ref-counting falls out for free.
- `Game.seeking_pause_accumulated_sec: int` — the one place an accumulator survives (see "Seeking-phase elapsed" below).
- `PauseReason` enum starts with `photo_question_open`; future features add values without schema changes.

```
pause(game, reason):
  if reason in active_pause_reasons: return  # idempotent
  if active_pause_reasons was empty: paused_at = now()
  active_pause_reasons.add(reason)
  emit GameTimerPausedEvent

resume(game, reason):
  if reason not in active_pause_reasons: return  # idempotent
  active_pause_reasons.remove(reason)
  if now empty:
    delta = now() - paused_at
    for d in [hiding_ends_at, found_claim_expires_at,
              *open_questions.deadline_at, *photo_deadlines]:
      if d is not None: d += delta
    seeking_pause_accumulated_sec += delta
    paused_at = None
    emit GameTimerResumedEvent
```

Transaction order in resume: shift deadlines first, clear `paused_at` last, single commit. The reconciler reads in its own transaction and either sees "still paused, skip" or "unpaused with already-shifted deadlines" — never an inconsistent middle. Every shifted deadline is provably ≥ now() at resume because the reconciler couldn't have fired it during pause (it filtered on `paused_at IS NULL`).

### Seeking-phase elapsed (the carve-out)

Seeking has no natural deadline — it ends on `found` / `host_ended` / `dissolved`, not a clock. So it can't be reframed into a future-date column. Solution: a dedicated `Game.seeking_pause_accumulated_sec`. Mobile reads `(seeking_started_at, seeking_pause_accumulated_sec, paused, paused_at)` and computes:

```
elapsed = now - seeking_started_at - seeking_pause_accumulated_sec
        - (paused ? now - paused_at : 0)
```

This is the only place pause-aware math lives client-side, and it's purely a UI value — never consumed by the reconciler.

### Reconciler

Each overdue query collapses from `(start_anchor + duration) ≤ now()` to `deadline_col ≤ now()`, plus `paused_at IS NULL`. Simpler than today.

### Events (mobile-driven)

Distinct events so mobile doesn't have to compare snapshots to detect transitions:
- `GameTimerPausedEvent { paused_at, active_pause_reasons }` — both channels.
- `GameTimerResumedEvent { resumed_at, active_pause_reasons, seeking_pause_accumulated_sec, hiding_ends_at?, found_claim_expires_at?, question_deadlines: dict[uuid, datetime] }` — both channels. Carries every shifted deadline so clients update their stores in one delta.

Snapshot fields (`HiderGameStateResponse` / `SeekerGameStateResponse`) gain `paused: bool`, `active_pause_reasons: list[PauseReason]`, `paused_at`, `seeking_pause_accumulated_sec`, plus the new deadline columns.

### Mobile impact

- `useCountdownTimer` is unchanged — it already counts to a future ISO. Question banners and the hiding belt timer both consume new deadline columns directly.
- `useGameTimer` collapses: hiding branch becomes a `useCountdownTimer` call against `hiding_ends_at`. Only the seeking-elapsed branch retains custom math (the three-input formula above), with a `paused` short-circuit on the 1s tick.
- Pause/resume events drive UI state changes (button enabling/disabling, timer color, banner) — TBD what specifically changes per game state, see follow-up.

### Trade-off vs shift-the-anchor

Slightly bigger schema migration (one new column per timer kind + backfill for in-flight games), but column names tell the truth, mutation-while-future is semantically uncontroversial, and audit history is preserved. The thing we're paying for — clarity of meaning — is exactly the property that motivated the reframe.
notes:
## Per-reason pause UX (2026-04-25)

Three structural categories of pause, distinguished by what's blocking and who can act. Each PauseReason maps to one category.

### 1. Role-targeted pause (banner UX)
The clock waits on a specific role's action.
- Non-interrupting banner on both sides naming what we're waiting on.
- The role being waited on retains full feature interactivity — the action that resolves the pause is the same one they'd take normally.
- The other role can strategize freely (preview endpoints, history, map, location reporting) but cannot start a new clock.

### 2. Universal pause — host-initiated (modal UX)
- Non-dismissable modal on every client: "The host has paused the game."
- All gameplay actions disabled.
- Host's modal additionally exposes "Resume" + "End Game" buttons (End ends the game from that point).
- No deadline; resolution is a host action.

### 3. Universal pause — rest period (modal UX, TBD)
- Non-dismissable modal with countdown to auto-resume.
- All gameplay actions disabled.
- Resolution is timer-driven; server auto-unpauses on `rest_period_ends_at`.
- Detailed mechanics deferred. First cut likely needs a separate auto-unpause column the reconciler reads despite the global `paused_at IS NULL` filter (rest-period unpause is a clock that fires *while* paused — the only such carve-out).

### In-scope reasons

| Reason | Category | Waiting on | Resolved by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_question_open` (HideAndSeek-nah) | Role-targeted | hider | Hider submits a photo that gets accepted (or review-timer auto-accept). |
| `host` (future) | Universal modal | — | Host taps Resume (or End Game). |
| `rest_period` (TBD) | Universal modal w/ countdown | — | Server auto-unpause on deadline. |

### Universal affordances during any pause

- Belt timer color: muted/grayscale (overrides green-when-connected).
- Belt timer value (count-up): frozen at last value.
- Active question deadline countdown: frozen at last value.
- Found-claim countdown: frozen at last value (modal stays open mid-flight; confirm/reject stays live — that resolves an existing clock, doesn't start a new one).
- Map / location reporting / history modals / endgame scrubber: stay live.
- New-clock-starting actions (ask question, start found-claim) disabled in all categories.
- Banner copy: reason-only, no elapsed-pause display (avoids anxiety, user can't act on it).

### `photo_question_open` specifics

- Already in scope: seeker can't ask new questions (active photo question gates that), so seeker side is no different from baseline except for the banner + frozen timer color.
- Hider side: power-ups disabled. Existing photo submit/answer affordances stay live (they resolve the pause).
- Both sides: banner reads e.g. "Paused — waiting on <hider name>'s photo."

### Resolutions of earlier open questions

- "Does the hider answer button freeze during pause?" — **yes if that flow is the resolution; otherwise no.** Photo submit stays live during `photo_question_open`; a hypothetical future "waiting on seeker" pause would freeze the answer button on the hider side and keep the seeker's resolving action live.
- "Found-claim resolution during pause?" — confirm/reject stays live. Only *initiating* a claim is disabled.
- "Hiding-phase pause?" — out of scope (hiding is a fixed countdown, no need).

### Implication for the data model

The category split lives in event metadata, not in extra columns. Mobile discriminates via the reason value plus the player's role + host-flag. Server stays simple:

- `Game.paused_at: datetime | None` — true when paused.
- `Game.active_pause_reasons: list[PauseReason]` (JSON) — idempotent set; empty ↔ non-empty drives the freeze/thaw transition. Sufficient for category 1 and category 2.
- For category 3 (rest period): defer until that feature is designed. Will likely add `Game.rest_period_ends_at: datetime | None` and a fourth reconciler query that fires an auto-unpause task while `paused_at IS NOT NULL`.

### `GameTimerPausedEvent` / `GameTimerResumedEvent`

- `paused`: `{ paused_at, active_pause_reasons }` — both channels.
- `resumed`: `{ resumed_at, active_pause_reasons (now empty if fully resumed, or reduced), seeking_pause_accumulated_sec, hiding_ends_at?, found_claim_expires_at?, question_deadlines: dict[uuid, datetime] }` — both channels.

A pause that adds a second reason (e.g. host-pause stacked on top of an in-flight photo pause) emits a `paused` event with the updated `active_pause_reasons` set so mobile re-evaluates which category UI to render. Mobile's category dispatch is: any host/rest-period reason in the set → modal; otherwise → banner.

title: Veto powerup: hider refuses to answer a question

- Trust-based: no card/hand tracking on server. Hider is assumed to have the powerup.
- Veto replaces the answer action — hider hits a veto endpoint instead of the answer endpoint.
- Auto-answer timer must be revoked when veto is played (same as normal answer).
- Question status should reflect that it was vetoed (new status? or answered with a special answer value?).
- Push notification to seekers: "The hider used a veto! No answer this time."
- The re-ask cost multiplier mechanic (questions can be asked more than once, cost doubles each time) is a prerequisite — may need its own implementation work.

Open questions:
- Should vetoed questions have a distinct status (e.g. `vetoed`) or use `answered` with `answer=null`?
- How to track ask count per question identity for cost multiplier?

title: Apply game-timer pause to photo questions
description:
Wire the game-timer pause mechanic (HideAndSeek-m8r) into the photo question lifecycle (HideAndSeek-z32) to close the bad-photo-spam exploit.

## Context

From design/2026-04-21-photo-questions.md §10:
> **Rejection exploitability is known and deferred.** A hider could submit bad photos repeatedly to burn seeker time. The planned mitigation is a game-timer-pause mechanic (separate bead) that freezes the seeking clock during open photo questions.

Until this task is done, hiders can trivially stall by submitting garbage photos on repeat — each rejection loops back to `asked` with a fresh submit window, and the seeking clock keeps running.

## Scope

- Call `pause_game(game, PauseReason.photo_question_open)` when a photo question transitions to `submitted`.
- Call `resume_game(game, PauseReason.photo_question_open)` on any terminal transition (`answered`, `vetoed`, `randomized`, `abandoned`) **or** on reject (loops back to `asked`, clock resumes until next submission).
- Actually — revisit: should the clock pause on `asked` too, to cover the submit-deadline window? That is the whole stalling vector. Leaning yes: pause on ask, resume on terminal. But that gives hiders a zero-cost "free time" every time a seeker asks. Probably: pause only on `submitted`, accept the limited stalling on the submit-deadline (bounded by photo_submit_min).
- Add `PauseReason.photo_question_open` enum value.
- **Push dispatch**: photo accept / reject / auto-accept / auto-submit routers (and the submit endpoint) call `pause_game` / `resume_game`; they must also dispatch `send_push.delay(...)` carrying the new `game_timer_paused` / `game_timer_resumed` event payload. Core only emits to SSE — push is a router-layer concern per the standard layering. Also extend the resume fan-out in `logic/pause.py` to shift `PhotoQuestionParams.submit_deadline_at` and `review_deadline_at` once those columns exist (the current TODO comment marks the site).
- Tests: multi-hider submit/reject cycles, submit-deadline expiry, auto-accept on review-deadline, veto during review.
- **Pause-shift coverage** (deferred from HideAndSeek-m8r.7): extend `server/tests/test_pause.py` with deadline-shift tests for `PhotoQuestionParams.submit_deadline_at` and `review_deadline_at` once those columns land. Add `paused_at IS NULL` filter tests to `find_overdue_photo_submissions` / `find_overdue_photo_reviews` in `server/tests/test_timers_reconciler.py`.

## Dependencies

- Depends on HideAndSeek-z32 (photo questions shipped)
- Depends on HideAndSeek-m8r (game-timer pause mechanic shipped)

title: Curses: hider powers that hinder seekers (enforceable + honor-based)
description:
A new category of hider power whose effect lands on the seeker, not on the map. Curses sit alongside existing hider powers in the Powers UI and give the hider a way to push back on pursuit.

The interesting design tension: some curses the server/client can mechanically enforce, others rely on good-faith compliance by the seeker (a player trust-mechanic, same spirit as the hiding phase). Both kinds should feel legitimate in the game — honor-based curses are a feature, not a fallback.

## Why

Right now the hider is passive: they run, they hide, they answer. Powers (e.g., hiding zone expansion) give a small active lever, but most of the game is reactive. Curses give the hider offensive tools and rebalance long late-game chases where the seeker has accumulated strong information.

## Two enforceability tiers

**Mechanically enforced** — server/client gate behavior:
- Disable a specific question type for N minutes (e.g., "no radar for 10 min")
- Lock the seeker's pending question timer for N minutes (delay the answer)
- Hide the seeker's own GPS dot from their map for N minutes
- Refund/destroy one of the seeker's question inventory slots
- Force a cooldown before the seeker's next question

**Honor-based (good-faith)** — the client shows a rule with a timer; seeker pledges to comply:
- Must travel only by [walking | bus | train] for N minutes
- Must stay within X meters of current location for N minutes
- Must photograph the next transit stop you pass
- Must not check the app (other than the curse banner) for N minutes
- Must take a specific themed route (e.g., "only north-bound transit")
- Silly-rule curses: wear a hat, speak in rhymes, narrate your moves aloud

The line between tiers is worth thinking about up front — some rules are mechanically enforceable in principle but only if we also add tracking features (e.g., "only buses" would need the client to watch GPS+transit data and flag violations). Default to honor-based when enforcement would require disproportionate infrastructure.

## Open design questions

- **Deck or menu?** Does the hider draw a random curse from a deck, or pick from a menu? Deck is more fun / more replayable; menu is more strategic. Random with reroll cost might be a middle path.
- **Inventory / economy**: curses per game, per hider, or shared pool? Cost relative to other powers (e.g., is a curse "free" or does it consume a question-worth of resource)? How does it interact with hiding zone expansion as the other existing power?
- **Stacking**: can multiple curses be active simultaneously? Probably yes, but with a cap to avoid lockout scenarios.
- **Seeker notification**: curse arrival is presumably a push + SSE event with a banner + timer on the seeker side. Needs a clear visual distinct from question events.
- **Griefing safeguards**: honor-based curses need to stay fun. Any rule that requires physical action (hats, rhymes) should be opt-in at game creation, not forceable mid-game by the hider, otherwise a bad hider can make the game miserable. Probably: map owner / game creator selects which honor-based curse categories are in the deck for their game.
- **Late-game dynamics**: curses shouldn't trivialize escape — consider whether curses are disabled or nerfed once the seeker is within some proximity threshold.
- **Veto?** Seeker has no veto in the current design (hider does for seeker questions). A curse-veto would defeat the mechanic. But some "get out of curse" resource (e.g., a token earned by correctly guessing location) might balance it.

## Likely component breakdown (children to file later)

- **Design doc** as the first child — this epic has a lot of open questions and needs to settle into a spec before implementation.
- models: `Curse` table (or union into a single powers table), `CurseType` enum, per-game config for enabled curse categories on the GameMap.
- core: apply-curse / expire-curse logic; broadcast `CurseAppliedEvent`, `CurseExpiredEvent`.
- server: endpoint for hider to cast a curse; guard on seeker endpoints for mechanically enforced curses (e.g., question-ask 409 when a "no-questions" curse is active).
- worker: Celery timer to expire curses (reuse the reconciler pattern).
- mobile hider: curses tab inside Powers UI, selection flow.
- mobile seeker: curse banner with timer, visually distinct from question banner; modal for honor-based rule details.
- game config: GameMap-level toggles for which honor-based curse categories are allowed.

## Relationship to existing work

- Powers UI already exists (see feedback_powers_naming.md) — curses live inside it as a new category or sibling section, not a new top-level utility.
- Toast severity rules (feedback_toast_severity.md) apply: curse arrival is an *event on you* for the seeker, probably a warning-tier surface (unlike neutral status changes).
- Hiding zone expansion is the existing power for reference — same plumbing (SSE + push, game-state flag, one-time per game).

title: Audit GET /games/{id} and GET /maps/{id} response sizes
description:
Both endpoints return everything in a single response and will grow with the data:

- GET /games/{id}: full inventory template (13 slots), all players, timing, timestamps. The inventory is static after game creation — no reason to re-send it every poll. Players rarely change after lobby.
- GET /maps/{id}: full boundary polygon (47+ pts), all district polygons (up to 144 pts each, 5 districts = ~450 pts), district_classes, full default_inventory. The boundary and districts are large geometry payloads that never change.

Consider:
1. Splitting static vs dynamic data (e.g., map geometry fetched once, game status polled frequently)
2. ETag/conditional GET for map data
3. Separate endpoints for heavy sub-resources (boundary, districts, inventory template)
4. Pagination or lazy loading for districts if maps grow to many districts

Not urgent for a single Seattle map and small games, but will matter if we add more maps or support larger player counts.
close_reason: Not a real concern — these endpoints are called infrequently

title: Mobile: Handle auto-assigned and ambiguous station election at phase transition
description: When the hiding phase ends and the station is auto_assigned or ambiguous, the mobile client needs to handle these transitions gracefully. Currently the stop selection UI (candidate stops, zone preview, Set Stop button) is tied to the hiding phase and clears on phase transition. For auto_assigned: the client should fetch and display the zone immediately (same as manual election). For ambiguous: the client should re-enter the stop selection flow during the seeking phase so hiders can resolve the ambiguity. Both cases need the phase_changed SSE delta (which carries station_election_status + hider_station_id) to drive the UI. See design/hider-station-election.md for spec.

title: Seeker: block map interaction while waiting on found-claim response
description:
When a seeker submits a found claim (`POST /games/{id}/found`), they're essentially declaring the game over from their side — they should not be able to pan/tap/ask questions on the map while waiting for hider confirmation or rejection.

Currently seekers have no UI feedback after submitting, and can continue interacting with the gameplay screen. This creates a confusing UX: the seeker is telling the hider 'game over' but still playing.

Proposal:
- Present a blocking (or semi-blocking) modal/sheet to the claiming seeker after `POST /found` returns 204
- Content: 'Waiting for hiders to confirm…' + the 2-minute countdown (server auto-dismisses at T+120s)
- Modal dismisses automatically when any of these SSE events arrive:
  - `found_claim_rejected` (seeker channel) → show rejection toast (already implemented), close modal
  - `game_ended` with `reason=found` (both channels) → navigate to recap (already implemented)
  - `found_claim_expired` (both channels) → show expiration toast (already implemented), close modal

Mirror pattern: hiders already have `FoundClaimModal` (`mobile/src/components/FoundClaimModal.tsx`) for the confirm/reject decision. This bead adds the symmetrical seeker-side waiting modal.

Store field: mirror `foundClaimPending` on GameplayStore for the seeker role (or repurpose the existing field).

Discovered during manual QA of HideAndSeek-035.
close_reason: Closed

title: Expand hiding zone powerup: increase hiding zone radius mid-game
description:
Hider plays a powerup to expand the hiding zone radius during the seeking phase. This makes it harder for seekers to narrow down the hider's location, since the candidate station pool grows and exclusion coverage becomes less effective relative to the larger zone.

Key design points:
- Trust-based: no card/hand tracking. Hider assumed to have the powerup.
- The hiding zone radius is currently implicit (derived from the hider's station and map geometry). This powerup would need an explicit radius override or multiplier on the game.
- Expansion should be a fixed increment or multiplier (e.g. +50%, or +X convention units). TBD what feels balanced.
- Can likely be played at any time during seeking, not just in response to a question.
- Affects candidate stations and endgame exclusion calculations — both use the hiding zone.
- Push notification to all players: "The hider has expanded the hiding zone!"
- Should there be a limit on how many times this can be played? (Probably trust-based — hider only has so many cards.)

Open questions:
- Fixed increment vs percentage multiplier for the expansion?
- Can it be stacked (played multiple times)?
- New endpoint: POST /games/{id}/expand-hiding-zone, or a generic powerup endpoint?
- How to store the override — new column on Game (e.g. hiding_zone_radius_multiplier)?
- Does the hider need to have reached seeking phase, or can they play it during hiding?
close_reason: Closed
