title: Question history utility (hider + seeker)
description:
Add per-role question history UI accessible via utility belt.

Hider: read-only modal showing chronological list of questions (type, params, answer). Non-interactive.

Seeker: scrubber timeline with standalone map showing cumulative exclusion (red see-through) through scrub point + current question's delta exclusion (solid question-color, not rendered under already-excluded areas). Question card shows type/params/answer at current position.

## Design rationale

A general in-app notification/toast system (originally beads-466) was explored and ruled out because existing visual affordances already command attention for question lifecycle events:
- Hiders see a colored bar during active questions (type, timer, answer buttons).
- Seekers see a banner for each active question with timer.
- On answer, the map updates.

So the user attention problem is already solved for question events. What's actually missing is a way to *review* past questions — hence this history utility. A narrow toast feature (beads-035) still covers non-obvious non-question events (player-left, host-change, zone-expanded).

## Key files

- mobile/src/components/QuestionCutoffModal.tsx — existing seeker endgame cutoff modal; reference for row rendering and map-with-exclusions pattern.
- mobile/src/components/utility-belt/UtilityBelt.tsx — utility belt container. Currently holds 'Powers' (hider) and 'Endgame' (seeker). New history entry slots in alongside.
- mobile/src/stores/GameplayStore — holds question_history array, already populated from SSE stream.
- core/src/hideandseek_core/broadcast/events.py — HiderQuestionAnsweredEvent / SeekerQuestionAnsweredEvent carry all needed data.

## Shared refactor

Extract a QuestionHistoryRow component from QuestionCutoffModal so all three surfaces render identically: seeker endgame cutoff, hider history modal, seeker scrubber question card.

## Data

question_history already in GameplayStore; per-question exclusion geometry already carried by SeekerQuestionAnsweredEvent — no new endpoints needed.

title: Migrate backend from AWS to self-hosted k3s homelab
description:
Rehost the HideAndSeek backend on the homelab k3s cluster after the AWS teardown on 2026-08-27. AWS was running ~$130/mo (RDS $46.54, ECS $29.42, ELB $16.74, ElastiCache $11.90, VPC $11.16 in July); all four CDK stacks were destroyed and there is currently NO live deployment.

Target stack (decided 2026-08-27):
- Runtime: k3s (replaces ECS Fargate + ALB)
- Ingress: Cloudflare Tunnel (replaces CloudFront + ACM + ALB)
- Postgres+PostGIS self-hosted (replaces Aurora Serverless v2)
- Redis self-hosted (replaces ElastiCache)
- Object storage: Garage, already running (replaces S3) — S3-compatible, and the code only uses put_object/get_object via an env-driven AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, so this is near config-only
- Push: KEEP AWS SNS Mobile Push (no good self-hosted equivalent). The two platform apps + apns/fcm secrets stay in AWS (~$0.80/mo)

Still deliberately in AWS: Route 53 zone marchese.dev, CDKToolkit bootstrap, SNS platform apps, hideandseek/apns-signing-key + hideandseek/fcm-service-account.

Known cross-cutting risks (each has a child): Cloudflare Tunnel requires the hostname be served by Cloudflare DNS while marchese.dev is in Route 53; SSE is long-lived and must be proven through the tunnel; ECS task roles are gone so SNS now needs a scoped long-lived IAM credential; Aurora's free 7-day backups and CloudWatch logs both need replacements.

This epic obsoletes or retargets several AWS-coupled beads — see the cleanup child.

title: Design: homelab k3s migration
description:
Write design/2026-08-27-homelab-migration.md. Must be self-contained per design/CLAUDE.md — do not defer to design/2026-04-19-aws-deployment.md as authoritative; incorporate the current state (AWS is torn down, nothing is live).

Cover: k3s topology (namespace, Deployments, resource requests/limits), how each AWS component maps to its replacement, secret handling, the Cloudflare Tunnel ingress path, Garage bucket layout, what stays in AWS and why, backup + observability story, and the cutover sequence.

Explicitly record which AWS-era design decisions no longer apply — chiefly the EventBridge timers design (design/2026-04-29-eventbridge-timers.md), whose entire motivation was Aurora Serverless v2 auto-pause cost.

title: Cloudflare Tunnel ingress to the k3s cluster
description:
Replaces CloudFront + ACM cert + ALB (was $16.74/mo for the ALB alone).

Run cloudflared in-cluster pointed at the server Service on :8000, and route hideandseek.marchese.dev through it. TLS terminates at Cloudflare, so the ACM certificate and its renewal disappear entirely.

Depends on the DNS move — the hostname must be served by Cloudflare DNS for tunnel routing to resolve.

Verify against the SSE spike before treating this as done: streaming behaviour is the thing most likely to break, and it is not visible in a simple curl of a JSON endpoint.

title: Point photo storage at Garage
description:
Replaces the S3 photo bucket (deleted during teardown; it was empty, so there is no data to migrate).

This should be close to config-only. The entire S3 surface is put_object + get_object in core/src/hideandseek_core/s3.py, both proxied through the server — no presigned URLs and no direct-to-bucket client uploads, which is where S3-compatible implementations usually diverge. get_s3_config() already reads AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, the same override LocalStack uses in docker-compose.

Work: create the Garage bucket and access key, set S3_BUCKET_NAME + AWS_ENDPOINT_URL + credentials on server/worker/reconciler, confirm boto3 signing works against Garage (check whether it needs path-style addressing), and round-trip a photo question end to end.

Consider pointing local dev at Garage too, replacing the LocalStack S3 half — closer dev/prod parity than the current split.

title: Scoped IAM user for SNS publish from homelab
description:
Push stays on AWS SNS Mobile Push, but the identity model changes. In ECS, three task roles supplied short-lived credentials automatically; outside AWS there is no task role, so the homelab needs a long-lived IAM access key. That is a real security downgrade and deserves tight scoping.

Recreate the least-privilege grants that app-stack.ts defined inline:
- server: sns:CreatePlatformEndpoint, sns:SetEndpointAttributes, sns:GetEndpointAttributes on the two platform-application ARNs, plus sns:Publish on their endpoint children
- worker: sns:Publish on endpoint children only (it never registers tokens)
- reconciler: no SNS permissions at all

Decide whether one user with the union of grants is acceptable or whether server and worker each get their own key. Plan for rotation — this credential now lives outside AWS and nothing rotates it automatically.

Platform app ARNs: arn:aws:sns:us-west-2:<account>:app/APNS/hideandseek-ios and .../app/GCM/hideandseek-android. Note app-stack.ts constructed these deterministically from account+region; whatever replaces it must do the same rather than hardcoding the account.

title: Postgres backup + restore for the homelab
description:
Aurora provided 7-day automated backups (backup: { retention: Duration.days(7) }) for free. Self-hosting means that guarantee is gone unless it is rebuilt — this is new work AWS was doing invisibly.

Needs: scheduled pg_dump or WAL archiving, off-cluster storage (Garage is an obvious target), retention policy, and — critically — a restore that has actually been exercised at least once. An untested backup is not a backup.

Not blocking first cutover (no production data exists yet — the Aurora data was discarded during teardown), but it must land before real games run against this deployment.

title: Log aggregation + basic alerting for the homelab
description:
CloudWatch Logs are gone. The stack logs via structlog through hideandseek_core.logging.setup_logging(), which is env-driven — ENV=production plus LOG_FORMAT=json produces structured JSON that a collector can parse without code changes.

Needs: somewhere for pod logs to land and be searchable, retention, and at minimum an alert when a pod is crash-looping or the server is unreachable. The AWS design leaned on a CloudWatch alarm as the safety net for timer delivery; whatever replaces it should cover the reconciler silently dying, since a stalled reconciler stops game timers without any user-visible error.

title: Retire the CDK app and update CLAUDE.md docs
description:
infra/cdk/ still describes infrastructure that no longer exists — all four stacks were destroyed 2026-08-27. It is now historical and actively misleading to a future session.

Decide: delete infra/cdk/ outright (git history preserves it) or move it to an archived path with a clear header stating it is dead. Use git mv if it moves, per feedback_git_mv.

Docs to update: root CLAUDE.md (drops the infra/cdk bullet, adds the homelab equivalent), infra/cdk/CLAUDE.md, design/2026-04-19-aws-deployment.md (mark superseded), and the pre-commit hook's cdk-checks step in hooks/pre-commit — which will otherwise keep running cdk synth against a deleted app and fail.

Also drop the now-pointless infra/cdk/.env requirement noted in feedback_worktree_env_copy — new worktrees have been needing that file solely to satisfy cdk synth.

title: Reconcile AWS-coupled beads against the homelab target
description:
The migration invalidates or retargets several existing issues. Work through them deliberately rather than letting them rot:

- HideAndSeek-fo0 (epic, EventBridge timer scheduling) + its plan child fo0.1 — the stated motivation was that 1Hz reconciler polling defeats Aurora Serverless v2 min=0 auto-pause, 'the single largest hobby-cost regression in the current deploy'. Self-hosted Postgres has no auto-pause and no per-ACU billing, so that rationale is gone entirely. Likely close as obsolete along with design/2026-04-29-eventbridge-timers.md. Note this was the most recent commit on dev — confirm with the user before closing.
- HideAndSeek-crr (Eager SNS delivery-failure handling via EventBridge/Lambda) — SNS stays, so the goal survives, but the EventBridge/Lambda mechanism does not. Either retarget at an SNS->SQS consumer polled from the homelab, or close in favour of the existing lazy cleanup (dead tokens are already reaped inline from sns:Publish responses).
- HideAndSeek-81h (Photo S3 cleanup lifecycle) — retarget from S3 lifecycle rules to Garage. The design already preferred a game-state-aware sweeper over bucket lifecycle rules, which is now the only option.
- HideAndSeek-pce (Seed Seattle map into production database) — still valid, retarget 'production' at the homelab DB. It also depends on the deployment existing, so it should block on this epic.

title: Cutover: deploy and smoke-test the homelab stack end to end
description:
The integration milestone — the point at which hideandseek.marchese.dev is live again.

Exercise the full path from a real device on cellular, not just from inside the LAN, since the whole point of the tunnel is public reachability:
- create game, join from a second device, colour assignment
- start game, confirm timers fire (this exercises the reconciler singleton and Celery through the self-hosted Redis)
- SSE: lobby events and gameplay events both stream and survive a multi-minute idle period
- push notification delivery through the retained AWS SNS path, from a homelab-hosted worker using the new IAM credential
- photo question submit + retrieve against Garage
- a pod restart mid-game, confirming state survives in Postgres and the client reconnects

Per feedback_deploy_before_ship, infra work stays uncommitted until a real deploy plus these smoke checks pass.

title: Move hideandseek.marchese.dev DNS to Cloudflare
description:
BLOCKER for the Cloudflare Tunnel ingress. Cloudflare Tunnel routes traffic by serving the hostname from Cloudflare's own DNS — a <tunnel-id>.cfargotunnel.com target only resolves inside Cloudflare DNS, so a CNAME from Route 53 will NOT work.

marchese.dev is currently a Route 53 hosted zone (3 records, kept deliberately through the AWS teardown).

Two options to evaluate:
1. Move the whole marchese.dev zone to Cloudflare. Cleanest, drops the last Route 53 charge (~$0.50/mo), but touches every other marchese.dev record.
2. Delegate only hideandseek.marchese.dev to Cloudflare via NS records in Route 53. Narrower blast radius, keeps the rest of the zone untouched, slightly more moving parts.

Per user_domains memory, marchese.dev is the cloud/public domain and may host other things — check what those 3 records point at before choosing.

title: Prove SSE survives Cloudflare Tunnel
description:
Risk-reduction spike. The app depends on long-lived Server-Sent Events streams (GET /games/{id}/lobby/events and the gameplay channel) — if Cloudflare Tunnel buffers or times these out, the ingress choice has to change and much of the migration reshapes.

Verify:
- A stream stays open well past Cloudflare's ~100s idle-connection behaviour; confirm whether the existing SSE keepalive cadence is enough or needs shortening.
- Events are flushed immediately, not buffered — Cloudflare proxies can buffer responses without Content-Type/cache hints; check text/event-stream passes through unbuffered.
- Reconnect/Last-Event-ID semantics still behave through the tunnel.
- Photo upload request body size limits (Cloudflare free tier caps request bodies at 100MB; check our max photo size sits well under).

Do this EARLY — before the manifests are finalised. A failure here means rethinking ingress, not tweaking config.

title: Self-host Postgres 16 + PostGIS on k3s
description:
Replaces Aurora Serverless v2 (was $46.54/mo — the single largest line item).

Requirements:
- Postgres 16 to match rds.AuroraPostgresEngineVersion.VER_16_6, with the PostGIS extension available (the schema uses ShapelyGeography/ShapelyGeometry columns and ST_Distance/ST_DWithin/ST_Contains).
- Persistent volume with a storage class that survives node restarts. This is now real state we own — Aurora's storage durability was free and is not any more.
- Decide operator vs plain StatefulSet (CloudNativePG is the obvious operator choice; a StatefulSet is simpler at one-node hobby scale).
- Credentials surfaced as DATABASE_URL in the postgresql+psycopg:// form the app expects.

Note the app's SQLAlchemy engine sets pool_pre_ping=True specifically to survive Aurora auto-resume — harmless to keep, but the comment explaining it is now stale.

title: Self-host Redis on k3s
description:
Replaces ElastiCache cache.t4g.micro (was $11.90/mo).

Redis carries two distinct workloads: the Celery broker, and the SSE pub/sub fan-out (get_sync_redis/get_async_redis in core). Both are non-durable — a Redis restart drops queued tasks and in-flight SSE subscriptions rather than corrupting game state, so persistence is optional but worth a deliberate decision rather than an accident.

Single instance is fine at hobby scale; no need to reproduce a replication group.

title: Container image build + registry for k3s
description:
Replaces the CDK DockerImageAsset + ECR flow. All three services (server, worker, reconciler) run the SAME image with different commands — preserve that.

Decide where images live: GHCR, a registry in-cluster, or k3s's containerd image import for a single-node cluster. Also decide how builds are triggered now that 'cdk deploy' no longer builds and pushes.

The us-west-2 CDK asset ECR repo still holds 6 images (818MB) from the AWS era — it can be emptied once this lands and nothing needs to roll back to it.

title: k3s manifests for server, worker, reconciler
description:
Replaces the three ECS Fargate services in HideAndSeek-App.

Port the per-service shape from infra/cdk/lib/app-stack.ts:
- server: uvicorn hideandseek.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000, was 512 CPU / 1024 MiB, exposes :8000
- worker: celery -A hideandseek_worker.celery_app worker, was 256 / 512, no port
- reconciler: python -m hideandseek_reconciler, was 256 / 512, no port

CRITICAL — the reconciler is a singleton. ECS enforced this with a 0/100 min/max deploy percentage so the old task always stopped before the new one started. The k8s equivalent is replicas: 1 with strategy type Recreate (NOT the default RollingUpdate, which briefly runs two pods and would double-fire timers). It tolerates a 30-60s gap because the overdue query catches up on the next tick, and its SIGTERM handling was audited in HideAndSeek-wos.2.

Server needs a readiness probe so the tunnel doesn't route to a pod that hasn't finished starting.

title: Alembic migration Job on k3s
description:
Replaces the DataStack one-shot ECS migrate task driven by a Lambda-backed CloudFormation custom resource (RunMigrationsFn + cr.Provider) — a lot of machinery that a k8s Job replaces outright.

Requirements:
- Runs 'uv run alembic upgrade head' from /app against DATABASE_URL, exactly as the ECS Migrate container did.
- Must complete BEFORE server/worker/reconciler start, mirroring docker-compose's depends_on: service_completed_successfully. Options: a Job gated by an init container that waits on it, a Helm pre-upgrade hook, or an initContainer running the migration directly on the server Deployment.
- Migrations are forward-only; there is no down path (the CDK custom resource made DELETE a no-op for the same reason).

Per feedback_no_manual_alembic_upgrade memory: schema apply is owned by the deployment mechanism, never run by hand. That rule carries over — the Job is the new owner.

title: Secret management for the homelab deployment
description:
Replaces AWS Secrets Manager (was $1.20/mo) and the ECS task-role/secret injection path.

Secrets needed by the workloads:
- Postgres credentials / DATABASE_URL
- Garage S3 access key + secret for the photo bucket
- AWS credentials for SNS publish (see the scoped-IAM-user child)
- APNs signing key + FCM service account — these currently live in AWS Secrets Manager as hideandseek/apns-signing-key and hideandseek/fcm-service-account and are consumed by the SNS platform applications, not by our code directly; confirm whether the app needs them at all once SNS stays in AWS.

Pick an approach that is safe to commit: sealed-secrets or SOPS keeps manifests in git, plain k8s Secrets do not. Note the repo-wide rule in infra/cdk/CLAUDE.md — no personal info, credentials, or account IDs in committed files — which applies to whatever replaces it.

title: Remove unused ios.config.googleMapsApiKey to unblock fresh expo prebuild
description:
Fresh \`expo prebuild\` (e.g. in a git worktree with no \`mobile/ios/\` directory) fails during \`pod install\` because react-native-maps@1.26.20's config plugin injects:

\`\`\`ruby
pod 'react-native-google-maps', path: File.dirname(\`node --print \"require.resolve('react-native-maps/package.json')\"\`)
\`\`\`

…but the package no longer ships a \`react-native-google-maps.podspec\`, so the build aborts.

The plugin only injects this when iOS Google Maps config is set. iOS in this app uses Apple Maps (per mobile/CLAUDE.md: 'Map provider: Platform default ... no provider prop on <MapView>'), so the keys at mobile/app.config.ts:27 (ios.config.googleMapsApiKey) and mobile/app.config.ts:41 (ios.config.googleMaps.apiKey) are unused.

## Fix

Remove both iOS Google Maps key references from mobile/app.config.ts. Keep the Android entry (Android does use Google Maps).

## Verification

In a fresh worktree (or after \`rm -rf mobile/ios\` in main):

1. \`set -a && source mobile/.env && set +a && cd mobile && npx expo run:ios\` — should complete prebuild + pod install + build cleanly.
2. Apple Maps still renders on iOS sim.
3. Android build (\`npx expo run:android\`) still loads Google Maps tiles.

## Workaround until fixed

Copy mobile/ios/ from main repo into the worktree to skip prebuild.
close_reason: Fix landed in edf66a7 (Add background location tracking on mobile, Apr 21). Verified today in a fresh dev-based worktree: npx expo run:ios completed prebuild + pod install + xcodebuild, simulator launched, Apple Maps renders, bot joined lobby via POST /games/join. One correction to the original diagnosis: the podspec injection is done by @expo/config-plugins's built-in Maps plugin (node_modules/@expo/config-plugins/build/ios/Maps.js line 124 — reads ios.config.googleMapsApiKey, injects 'pod react-native-google-maps'), NOT react-native-maps's own plugin (which injects 'react-native-maps/Google' and wasn't firing). Useful to know if this regresses on a future Expo SDK bump. mobile/CLAUDE.md 'Working from a Git Worktree' section updated in 2c10544 to drop the 'copy mobile/ios/' workaround.

title: wos.5 follow-up: app SGs have no IPv4 egress to dbSg/redisSg
description: ServerSg/WorkerSg/ReconcilerSg in NetworkStack use allowAllOutbound=false with only allowAllIpv6Outbound=true. description:
Several API responses return fields that are always null/meaningless in context:

1. **QuestionDetailResponse (write endpoints)**: When returned from ask/answer POSTs, fields like seeker_location_end, hider_location, answered_at, answer are all null on ask, and seeker_location_end is null for non-thermometer types always. 3. **GameResponse nulls in early states**: hiding_started_at and seeking_started_at are null in lobby/hiding. join_code persists into seeking (should be nulled at transition — it already is in the DB but only when the game ends, not at seeking start).

These are cosmetic but they make the API feel unpolished and force the client to handle many null cases that conceptually can't happen.

title: Add debug-keystore SHA-1 to Android API keys for local expo run:android builds
description:
Follow-up to HideAndSeek-wos.10 and Maps SDK setup. Both Android API keys (Firebase auto-created key + Android Maps SDK key) are currently restricted to the production keystore SHA-1 only, so local 'npx expo run:android' builds — signed with ~/.android/debug.keystore — fail both FCM registration and Google Maps tile loading.

Prereq: actually wanting to iterate on Android locally (currently focused on iOS).

Steps:
1. Get debug keystore SHA-1: keytool -list -v -keystore ~/.android/debug.keystore -alias androiddebugkey -storepass android -keypass android | grep SHA1
   (If keystore missing, run 'npx expo run:android' once to generate it, then re-run keytool.)
2. Google Cloud Console → APIs & Services → Credentials → edit 'Android Maps SDK key' → Application restrictions → Android apps → add a second item with package 'dev.marchese.hideandseek' + the debug SHA-1. Save.
3. Same edit for 'Android key (auto created by Firebase)' if local FCM is wanted. Optional — push isn't needed for most local UI work.
4. Rebuild: cd mobile && npx expo run:android. Maps tiles should render; FCM should register if step 3 done.

Notes:
- Each dev machine has its own debug keystore with a different SHA-1; for a solo hobby project, just adding your own is fine. If we add other devs, switch to a separate dev-only key with looser restrictions rather than pinning every machine's debug SHA-1.
- Restriction propagation is typically <1 min, up to 5.

title: Hider question history modal (read-only)
description:
Add a utility belt entry for hiders that opens a modal listing all past questions in chronological order. Each row: question-type icon, Q-number, parameter summary, answer.

Non-interactive — purely informational reference for the hider. (Compare with the seeker's endgame cutoff modal, which renders the same row layout but is tappable to set a cutoff.)

## Where it lives

mobile/src/components/utility-belt/UtilityBelt.tsx — the hider utility belt currently holds 'Powers' (expand hiding zone, etc.). Add the history entry alongside.

## Reference implementation

title: Deploy HideAndSeek to production
description:
Get the HideAndSeek stack deployed to a real hosted environment so external users can play.

## Scope
The monorepo currently runs locally via docker compose (PostGIS + Redis + FastAPI + Celery worker + reconciler) and mobile via Expo dev builds. This epic covers everything needed to move that to a hosted deployment:

- **Backend hosting**: pick a platform (Fly.io, Railway, Render, AWS ECS, GKE, etc.) and deploy the FastAPI server, Celery worker, and reconciler services.
- **Database**: managed PostGIS (RDS, Supabase, Neon-with-postgis, Crunchy Bridge, etc.) with backups and migrations strategy.
- **Redis**: managed Redis (Upstash, ElastiCache, etc.) for Celery broker + SSE pub/sub.
- **Secrets/config**: DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, APNs key, FCM service account, etc. — pick a secret store.
- **CI/CD**: build + deploy pipeline (GitHub Actions → registry → platform).
- **Domain + TLS**: register domain, wire DNS, terminate TLS.
- **Observability**: logs, metrics, error tracking (Sentry?), uptime checks.
- **Mobile distribution**: EAS build + submit for TestFlight / Play internal testing; point app at hosted API URL via env config.
- **Push credentials in prod**: production APNs key + FCM service account wired into hosted env.
- **GTFS data pipeline**: how/when the Seattle GTFS import runs against the prod DB.
- **Smoke/manual tests against hosted env**: adapt `scripts/manual-test.sh` to run against a staging URL.

## Out of scope (for now)
- Multi-region / HA beyond what the chosen platform gives by default
- Autoscaling tuning (basic fixed sizing is fine for first deploy)
- Public launch / marketing

## Deliverable
A documented, reproducible deployment where a fresh clone + a few commands (or a merged PR) results in a running staging environment reachable by a TestFlight/internal-track build of the mobile app.
design:

title: Logging audit: server, worker, reconciler
description:
Unify logging across server, worker, and reconciler. Scoped from the 2026-04-19 audit to infrastructure-level changes only; business-logic log coverage is tracked separately in HideAndSeek-j8u.

## Scope (single plan → implement cycle)

### 1. Move setup_logging() from server to core
- Relocate `server/src/hideandseek/logging.py` → `core/src/hideandseek_core/logging.py`
- Server `main.py` lifespan calls the shared setup
- Worker wires it via Celery's `celeryd_init` (or equivalent) signal so --loglevel isn't the source of truth
- Reconciler `__main__.py` calls it before entering the poll loop
- Drop `--loglevel=info` from the compose worker command

### 2. Route SQLAlchemy through structlog
- Leave `create_engine(...)` with `echo=False`
- In setup_logging(), set `logging.getLogger('sqlalchemy.engine')` to INFO when ENV=local, WARNING otherwise
- Optional: `SQL_ECHO` env var to force it on in production temporarily

### 3. Standardize levels across all three services
- local: root DEBUG, sqlalchemy.engine INFO, console renderer
- production: root INFO, sqlalchemy.engine WARNING, JSON renderer, uvicorn access WARNING
- Third-party (aioapns, firebase_admin, httpx, asyncio) pinned to WARNING both modes
- Single ENV + LOG_FORMAT env-var pair drives all three containers

- Adding logs to core/logic/ and core/queries/ (see HideAndSeek-j8u)
- CloudWatch wiring (lands with wos.8 AppStack)
- Changing the access-log middleware — it stays as-is

All three items edit the same setup_logging() module and core/db.py; splitting creates awkward intermediate states (a shared logging module that doesn't route SQL yet, or routes SQL but doesn't have standardized levels).

title: Photo questions: hider-submitted images as evidence
description:
Add a new `photo` question type. The seeker requests a photo of a specific subject (tree, building, sign, etc.); the hider's app captures and uploads an image; the photo is shown to the seeker as human-interpretable evidence. No map exclusion — value is purely informational (urban vs. rural, terrain, density, signage clues).

## Why this is interesting

Existing question types (radar, thermometer, matching, measuring, tentacles) all reduce the search area via geometry. Photo questions are the first type whose payoff is *qualitative* — the seeker reasons about the image rather than the map. This adds a different cognitive lever and makes the game feel less like a pure geometric puzzle.

## Design surface (open questions, not decisions)

- **Subject vocabulary**: a fixed enum of allowed subjects (tree, building, sign, road, sky, vehicle, water, etc.) vs. free-form text. Fixed enum is simpler, fairer, and avoids prompts that effectively leak GPS ("photo of the Space Needle"). Probably start fixed.
- **Multi-hider behavior**: who answers when there are multiple hiders? Likely consistent with how other question types resolve answers across hiders — needs to be confirmed against `logic/answer.py`.
- **Storage**: S3 bucket with server-issued presigned PUT (hider upload) and presigned GET (seeker view). CDK stack adds the bucket + IAM. LocalStack supports S3 for dev.
- **Lifetime**: photos tied to game lifecycle; delete on game end / dissolution. (Keep history briefly for question-history feature.)
- **Anti-cheat**: do we trust the hider's camera roll, or require live capture? Live capture (expo-camera, no library picker) is the honest default. EXIF stripping on upload to avoid leaking GPS to the seeker accidentally — wait, actually we *want* the visual content but not the metadata coordinates; strip EXIF server-side.
- **Compression**: cap dimensions / re-encode to keep bandwidth + storage bounded.
- **Veto/abandon**: same lifecycle as other questions; if hider doesn't upload within timer, question is abandoned.

## Likely component breakdown (children to file later)

- models: `QuestionType.photo`, `PhotoQuestionParams` (subject category, S3 object key, uploaded_at), maybe a `PhotoSubject` enum.
- core: ask + answer logic; broadcast `PhotoQuestionAskedEvent` / `PhotoQuestionAnsweredEvent` (answer carries presigned GET URL or object key).
- server: presigned upload URL endpoint; serve presigned GET in the answer event; S3 client wiring + config.
- mobile: hider capture flow (expo-camera), upload via presigned PUT, seeker photo viewer modal.

## Notes

- Seeker's existing question UI will need to gain a non-geometric question card (no exclusion delta on the map; result is the image).

title: Photo questions: data model + default inventory
description:
## Scope

Foundation cycle for photo questions: enums, ORM model, Alembic migration, inventory default expansion. Everything downstream depends on this.

See `design/2026-04-21-photo-questions.md` §4 (Data Model) and §2 (Subject vocabulary). S3 plumbing is cycle 2 (separate bead).

### Enums

- `QuestionType.photo` — add to existing enum.
- `QuestionStatus.submitted` — add (new non-terminal state between `asked` and `answered`).
- `PhotoSubject` (StrEnum, 18 values, per design §2):
  - small-gated: `tree`, `sky`, `selfie`, `widest_street`, `tallest_structure_in_sightline`, `any_building_from_station`
  - medium-gated: `tallest_building_from_station`, `nearest_street_trace`, `two_buildings`, `restaurant_interior`, `train_platform`, `park`, `grocery_aisle`, `place_of_worship`
  - large-gated: `half_mile_streets_traced`, `tallest_mountain_from_station`, `biggest_body_of_water`, `five_buildings`
- `PhotoReviewDecision` (StrEnum): `accepted`, `rejected`, `auto_accepted`.
- `PhotoSubjectMeta` dataclass: `label: str`, `min_size: MapSize`. Populated in a `PHOTO_SUBJECT_META: dict[PhotoSubject, PhotoSubjectMeta]` keyed by `PhotoSubject`.
- Helper: `subjects_for_size(size: MapSize) -> list[PhotoSubject]` — returns subjects with `min_size <= size`. `MapSize.special` returns empty (never user-selectable).

### Table: `PhotoQuestionParams`

One-to-one with `Question`, co-located with the other per-type params tables in models:

```python
class PhotoQuestionParams(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'photo_question_params'
    question_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey('question.id', ondelete='CASCADE'), primary_key=True
    )
    subject: Mapped[PhotoSubject]
    photo_object_key: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(default=None)
    is_null_answer: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(default=False)
    submitted_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(default=None)
    submitted_by: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey('player.id'), default=None
    )
    review_decision: Mapped[PhotoReviewDecision | None] = mapped_column(default=None)
    reviewed_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(default=None)
    reviewed_by: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey('player.id'), default=None
    )
    question: Mapped[Question] = relationship(back_populates='photo_params')
```

Add corresponding relationship on `Question`:
```python
photo_params: Mapped[PhotoQuestionParams | None] = relationship(
    back_populates='question', uselist=False,
)
```

### Column additions

- `Game.photo_submit_min: Mapped[int | None]` (nullable — defaults cascade via helper).
- `Game.photo_review_sec: Mapped[int | None]` (nullable).
- `GameMap.default_photo_submit_min: Mapped[int | None]`.
- `GameMap.default_photo_review_sec: Mapped[int | None]`.
- `InventorySlot.photo_subject: Mapped[PhotoSubject | None]` (nullable — only set for `question_type=photo` slots).

### Effective helpers (in `core/`, colocated with `effective_hiding_zone_radius_m`)

```python
DEFAULT_PHOTO_SUBMIT_MIN: dict[MapSize, int] = {
    MapSize.small: 10, MapSize.medium: 10, MapSize.large: 20,
}
DEFAULT_PHOTO_REVIEW_SEC = 30

def effective_photo_submit_min(game: Game) -> int:
    if game.photo_submit_min is not None:
        return game.photo_submit_min
    if game.game_map.default_photo_submit_min is not None:
        return game.game_map.default_photo_submit_min
    return DEFAULT_PHOTO_SUBMIT_MIN[game.size]

def effective_photo_review_sec(game: Game) -> int:
    if game.photo_review_sec is not None:
        return game.photo_review_sec
    if game.game_map.default_photo_review_sec is not None:
        return game.game_map.default_photo_review_sec
    return DEFAULT_PHOTO_REVIEW_SEC
```

### Inventory expansion (`core/src/hideandseek_core/conventions.py`)

`get_default_inventory(convention, size)` currently seeds `InventorySlot`s for the existing five types. Extend to emit **one `InventorySlot` per `PhotoSubject` whose `min_size <= size`** with `question_type=QuestionType.photo`, a unique `slot_index`, and `photo_subject=<subject>`. No distance fields — photo slots only populate `photo_subject`.

Expected slot counts:
- small map: 6 photo slots.
- medium map: 14 photo slots.
- large map: 18 photo slots.

### Alembic migration

```bash
uv run alembic revision --autogenerate -m "Add photo question type"
```

Review the autogenerated migration. Postgres-specific considerations:

- `QuestionType` + `QuestionStatus` are existing enum types — adding values needs `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE` (cannot run inside a transaction). Follow whatever pattern prior enum-extension migrations used (inspect `alembic/versions/` for precedent — probably `op.execute("COMMIT")` or splitting the revision).
- `PhotoSubject` + `PhotoReviewDecision` are new enums — straightforward create.
- `photo_question_params` table with two FK cascades.
- Nullable column additions on `game`, `game_map`, `inventory_slot` — fast and non-blocking.

### Re-seed Seattle (dev DB only)

`GameMap.default_inventory` is stored as JSON at map-seed time (server/scripts/seed_seattle_map.py:658). Existing seeded maps won't gain photo slots until reseeded. For dev:

```bash
docker compose down -v
docker compose up --build -d postgres
cd server && uv run alembic upgrade head
uv run python scripts/import_seattle_gtfs.py
uv run python scripts/seed_seattle_map.py
```

No data migration needed — reseed is cheaper than throwaway JSON-mangling migration code. Document in the migration docstring that existing deployments should reseed.

## QA

Automated:
- `cd models && uv run ruff check . && uv run pyright`
- `cd core && uv run ruff check . && uv run pyright`
- `cd server && uv run alembic upgrade head` on fresh DB succeeds.
- `cd server && uv run pytest` — existing tests should not regress (photo isn't exercised yet).

Manual:
- Reseed Seattle; `psql` inspection of a seeded `GameMap.default_inventory` JSON:
  - Medium map → 14 photo slots covering small+medium subjects.
  - Large map → 18 photo slots.
- New enum values present in `pg_type`, new columns exist with expected nullability.
- Create a game from the seeded map and confirm its `InventorySlot` rows include photo slots with `photo_subject` populated.

## Out of scope

- Ask/submit/fetch logic (cycle 3, 4).
- S3 config + bucket (cycle 2).
- Any HTTP routes or events.
- Any client-side work.

title: Photo questions: S3 plumbing (config + CDK + LocalStack)
description:
## Scope

Blob-storage plumbing so cycles 4+ can read/write photos. Design refs: §5.1, §5.4, §5.5, §5.6.

Independent of cycle 1 — could proceed in parallel — but expected to land in order for cleaner CLAUDE.md updates and manual-QA sequencing.

### `core/src/hideandseek_core/config.py` — `S3Config`

Follow the `SnsConfig` pattern:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class S3Config:
    bucket_name: str
    endpoint_url: str | None  # LocalStack dev; None in prod

def load_s3_config() -> S3Config | None:
    """Return None if S3_BUCKET_NAME is missing — photo endpoints will 500/503 in that state."""
```

Env vars:
- `S3_BUCKET_NAME` (required).
- `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` (optional; already used by SNS — shared LocalStack endpoint).

Unlike `SnsConfig`, there's no useful no-op mode for S3. If the bucket is missing, photo questions cannot function. Server should surface a clean 500/503 on photo endpoints (added in cycle 4) rather than silently drop writes.

### S3 client module (`core/src/hideandseek_core/s3.py` — new file)

Typed thin wrapper over boto3's S3 client:

```python
def get_s3_client(config: S3Config) -> S3Client:
    """@cache-decorated factory, like get_sns_client."""

def upload_bytes(config: S3Config, key: str, body: bytes | BinaryIO, content_type: str) -> None:
    """Put an object into the bucket."""

def get_object_stream(config: S3Config, key: str) -> tuple[StreamingBody, str, int]:
    """Return (body stream, content_type, content_length). Caller must consume/close."""

def delete_object(config: S3Config, key: str) -> None:
    """Best-effort delete; idempotent (DeleteObject returns 204 even if missing)."""
```

Use `boto3-stubs[s3]` (`mypy_boto3_s3.S3Client`) for typing — no Any escape hatches per user preference.

### Dependency

Add `boto3-stubs[s3]` to `core/pyproject.toml`. boto3 is already present (SNS).

### CDK (`infra/cdk/`) — `DataStack`

New construct in `DataStack` (where Aurora + ElastiCache already live):

```ts
const photoBucket = new s3.Bucket(this, 'PhotoBucket', {
  bucketName: `hideandseek-photos-${props.env}`,
  encryption: s3.BucketEncryption.S3_MANAGED,
  versioned: false,
  publicReadAccess: false,
  blockPublicAccess: s3.BlockPublicAccess.BLOCK_ALL,
  removalPolicy: cdk.RemovalPolicy.RETAIN, // photos kept forever per design §10
});

// Expose to AppStack
this.photoBucket = photoBucket;
```

In `AppStack`:
- `photoBucket.grantReadWrite(taskDefinition.taskRole)` for api + worker.
- Pass bucket name as env var `S3_BUCKET_NAME=<bucket.bucketName>` to api/worker services (reconciler too — for eventual cleanup tasks; no cost to adding it now).

No CloudFront, no lifecycle rules, no versioning.

### LocalStack bootstrap (`infra/localstack/init-aws.sh`)

Append to the existing hook (which currently creates the SNS platform apps):

```bash
awslocal s3 mb s3://hideandseek-photos-local
```

### docker-compose (`docker-compose.yml`)

Add env vars to api, worker, reconciler services:
- `S3_BUCKET_NAME=hideandseek-photos-local`
- `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL=http://localstack:4566` (already present for SNS — confirm it's shared).

### CLAUDE.md updates

- `core/CLAUDE.md` — add S3Config + s3.py module to the config/module list.
- `infra/cdk/CLAUDE.md` — note the new bucket in DataStack.
- Root `CLAUDE.md` — add S3 bucket to the docker-compose service list if needed.

- `cd infra/cdk && npm run build`.

Manual:

- `awslocal s3 ls` shows `hideandseek-photos-local`.
- `awslocal s3 cp /tmp/test.jpg s3://hideandseek-photos-local/test/x.jpg` then `awslocal s3 cp s3://hideandseek-photos-local/test/x.jpg /tmp/test-dl.jpg` — bytes round-trip.

title: Photo questions: ask flow (server)
description:
## Scope

Seeker-initiated ask flow. No upload yet (cycle 4), no review (cycle 5), no mobile (cycles 6/7).

Design refs: §6.1 (ask), §6.6 (no preview), §6.7 (`PhotoEventParams` only).

### Logic (`core/src/hideandseek_core/logic/ask.py`)

New `ask_photo()` mirroring the existing `ask_*` functions:

```python
def ask_photo(
    game: Game,
    player: Player,
    seeker_location: Point,
    slot: InventorySlot,
) -> Question:
    """Create a photo question. Immediately asked; submit timer starts now."""
    assert slot.photo_subject is not None
    assert slot.question_type == QuestionType.photo
    slot.ask_count += 1

    question = register(
        Question(
            game=game,
            sequence=get_question_count(game) + 1,
            question_type=QuestionType.photo,
            status=QuestionStatus.asked,
            asked_by=player.id,
            seeker_location_start=seeker_location,
            ask_count=slot.ask_count,
            slot_index=slot.slot_index,
            answerable_at=datetime.now(UTC),  # submit timer anchor
            photo_params=PhotoQuestionParams(subject=slot.photo_subject),
        )
    )
    _log_question_asked(game, player, question)
    return question
```

Note: `answerable_at` doubles as the submit-timer anchor for the reconciler query in cycle 5 (`answerable_at + effective_photo_submit_min < now`).

### Request schema (`server/src/hideandseek_server/schemas/request.py`)

```python
class AskPhotoQuestionRequest(BaseModel):
    slot_index: int
```

Nothing fancier — photo questions have no custom_distance, no location-sensitive params beyond the seeker's current position (captured by the existing `get_seeker_in_game` + location dependency and logged via `seeker_location_start`).

### Router (`server/src/hideandseek_server/routers/questions.py`)

`POST /games/{game_id}/questions/photo`:

1. Auth: seeker-in-game (existing dependency).
2. Game must be in seeking phase, not terminal.
3. Validate `slot_index`:
   - Exists on game.
   - `question_type == photo`.
   - `photo_subject` non-null.
4. Call `ask_photo(game, player, seeker_location, slot)`.
5. Emit `QuestionAskedEvent` (existing event type) with `PhotoEventParams`.
6. Return the standard question response schema.

### Events (`core/src/hideandseek_core/broadcast/events.py`)

```python
class PhotoEventParams(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
    type: Literal['photo'] = 'photo'
    subject: PhotoSubject
```

Changes:
- Add `PhotoEventParams` to the `QuestionEventParams` discriminated union.
- Extend `build_event_params(question)` with:
  ```python
  case QuestionType.photo:
      assert question.photo_params is not None
      return PhotoEventParams(subject=question.photo_params.subject)
  ```

Client-side labels are looked up from a mobile-side `PhotoSubject -> str` map (cycle 6/7) — the wire doesn't carry labels.

### Preview wiring (`logic/preview.py` + preview router)

Photo questions skip preview. Dispatch in `preview_question()` (or the per-type preview map) should raise a 422 for `QuestionType.photo` with a clear error: "photo questions have no preview; use POST /questions/photo to ask directly."

### OpenAPI + SSE types

The pre-commit hook regenerates `openapi/openapi.yaml` and `mobile/src/api/schema.d.ts`. Confirm after commit:
- `openapi/openapi.yaml` contains `PhotoEventParams` under the `QuestionEventParams` union.
- `mobile/src/api/schema.d.ts` picks up the new type.
- `mobile/src/types/gameplay.ts` short aliases — extend if needed so the mobile cycles have clean imports.

## QA

Automated:
- `cd core && uv run ruff check . && uv run pyright`.
- `cd server && uv run ruff check . && uv run pyright`.
- `cd server && uv run pytest` — add at minimum:
  - Unit test for `ask_photo()`: asserts question row state, ask_count increment, PhotoQuestionParams presence + subject.
  - Router test: 200 on valid slot, 422 on wrong slot type (radar slot), 404 on nonexistent slot, 403 on non-seeker.
  - Event emission test: `QuestionAskedEvent` fires with `PhotoEventParams` on both SSE channels.

Manual smoke via docker compose:
1. Bring up stack (`docker compose up --build`) with a reseeded Seattle map (cycle 1 should have done this).
2. Create a game on medium map → seeding game carries photo inventory in `InventorySlot`.
3. Promote to seeking phase (skip hiding with dev helper or wait it out).
4. `psql` — pick a photo `slot_index` (say a `tree` slot).
5. `curl -H 'X-Player-Id: ...' -H 'X-Player-Secret: ...' -d '{"slot_index": N}' POST /games/{id}/questions/photo` → 201 with question id + PhotoEventParams on the response.
6. Two SSE streams open (hider-state + seeker-state). Confirm `QuestionAskedEvent` arrives on both with `parameters: {type: 'photo', subject: 'tree'}`.
7. `SELECT * FROM question WHERE id = ...` shows `question_type=photo`, `status=asked`, `answerable_at` ~= now. `SELECT * FROM photo_question_params WHERE question_id = ...` shows subject populated, all other cols null/default.
8. `curl -X POST /games/{id}/questions/{qid}/preview` → 422.
9. Ask again with the same slot → ask_count increments; new question row created.

## Dependencies

- Cycle 1 (models + inventory).

## Out of scope

- Submit, queue, null, fetch (cycle 4).
- Accept, reject, auto-resolve, push events (cycle 5).
- Mobile (cycles 6/7).

title: Photo questions: submit/queue + fetch (server)
description:
## Scope

Hider-facing upload/queue/null endpoints, state-sensitive fetch endpoint, `PhotoQueuedEvent`, `PhotoSubmittedEvent`, and the server side of the submission lock. Auto-resolve (reconciler/worker) is cycle 5; accept/reject is cycle 5.

Design refs: §5.2 (keys), §5.3 (endpoints + fetch auth), §6.2 (submit + lock), §6.7 (queued + submitted events), §8.7 (submission lock semantics).

### Upload/submit endpoint

`POST /games/{game_id}/questions/{question_id}/photo` — hider-in-game.

One endpoint handles photo upload, queue, and null answer. Dispatch on Content-Type:

- **multipart/form-data**:
  - `file`: image bytes (JPEG or PNG only — validate Content-Type and magic-byte sniff; reject others with 415).
  - `submit`: `'true'` | `'false'`.
- **application/json**:
  - `{"null": true}` — implicit submit=true (queuing a null is meaningless; one transition).

Server flow:
1. Auth: hider-in-game.
2. Validate: question exists, `game_id` matches path, `question_type == photo`, `status == asked`. If `status == submitted`: 409 (submission lock). If anything else: 409 with status name.
3. **Photo path**:
   - Generate key: `{env}/{game_id}/{uuid4}.{ext}` — `{env}` from `HIDEANDSEEK_ENV` with fallback `local`, `{ext}` is `jpg` or `png` based on validated content-type.
   - Upload bytes via `upload_bytes()` (cycle 2).
   - If `params.photo_object_key` already set, **leave the old key orphaned in S3** (kept forever per §10). Don't delete.
   - Set `params.photo_object_key = new_key`, `params.is_null_answer = False`.
   - Emit `PhotoQueuedEvent` to **hider channel only**. Fires on every upload (initial or replace).
4. **Null path**:
   - Set `params.is_null_answer = True`, `params.photo_object_key = None`.
   - No `PhotoQueuedEvent` for null — no thumbnail to show.
5. If `submit=true` (photo) or null path: call `_submit_photo_question(question, player)` → transitions to `submitted`, sets `submitted_at`/`submitted_by`, emits `PhotoSubmittedEvent` to **both channels**.
6. Return 204.

### `_submit_photo_question` (logic)

Place in a new file `core/src/hideandseek_core/logic/photo.py` (keeps photo-specific transitions co-located; avoids bloating `logic/answer.py`):

```python
def _submit_photo_question(question: Question, player: Player) -> None:
    params = question.photo_params
    assert params is not None
    assert question.status == QuestionStatus.asked
    # Caller must have set photo_object_key or is_null_answer before calling.
    assert params.photo_object_key is not None or params.is_null_answer
    params.submitted_at = datetime.now(UTC)
    params.submitted_by = player.id
    question.status = QuestionStatus.submitted
    logger.info(
        'photo_submitted',
        game_id=str(question.game_id),
        question_id=str(question.id),
        null=params.is_null_answer,
        submitted_by=str(player.id),
    )
```

### Unqueue endpoint

`DELETE /games/{game_id}/questions/{question_id}/photo` — hider-in-game.

Clears the queued photo:
- Requires `status == asked` (409 otherwise).
- `params.photo_object_key = None`, `params.is_null_answer = False`.
- **Open decision, flag during implementation** — emit unqueued signal as either:
  - (a) `PhotoQueuedEvent` with `queued_by=None`, `uploaded_at=None` (null-thumbnail variant), or
  - (b) A new `PhotoUnqueuedEvent` type.
  
  Prefer (b) for clarity and simpler client dispatch. Update design doc §6.7 if we go with (b).
- Do **not** delete the S3 object (consistent with "photos kept forever" per §10; avoids branching on reject vs unqueue).

### Fetch endpoint

`GET /games/{game_id}/questions/{question_id}/photo`:

Auth is state-sensitive (design §5.3):
- `status == asked` (photo queued pre-submit): **hiders only**. Seekers get 403.
- `status ∈ {submitted, answered, vetoed, randomized, abandoned}`: **any player in the game**.

Response:
- `Content-Type`: `image/jpeg` or `image/png` (stored or inferred from key extension).
- `Content-Length`: from S3 `get_object_stream` tuple.
- `Cache-Control: private, max-age=3600` — safe because the key is immutable per question (rejects clear the key, replacements mint a new key).
- Body: streamed S3 bytes via FastAPI `StreamingResponse(body_iter)`.

Special cases:
- `params.is_null_answer == True`: 404 with message "no photo for null answer."
- `params.photo_object_key is None` in asked state (pre-upload): 404.

Proxying (rather than presigning) buys central auth, fully private bucket, and stable URLs for question history. Bandwidth cost is fine at hobby scale.

### Events (`core/src/hideandseek_core/broadcast/events.py`)

```python
class PhotoQueuedEvent(GameplayEventSchema):
    question_id: uuid.UUID
    sequence: int
    queued_by: uuid.UUID | None  # None if unqueued (if we pick variant (a))
    uploaded_at: datetime | None  # None if unqueued
    # photo_object_key intentionally omitted — clients fetch via GET

class PhotoSubmittedEvent(GameplayEventSchema):
    question_id: uuid.UUID
    sequence: int
    status: QuestionStatus  # always 'submitted'
    submitted_at: datetime
    submitted_by: uuid.UUID | None  # NULL if auto-submitted from queue (cycle 5)
    is_null_answer: bool
    review_deadline: datetime
    # photo_object_key intentionally omitted — clients fetch via GET
```

`review_deadline = submitted_at + timedelta(seconds=effective_photo_review_sec(game))`, computed at emit time.

Channel routing in `broadcast/emit.py`:
- `PhotoQueuedEvent` — hider channel only (seekers have no need to see queue state).
- `PhotoSubmittedEvent` — both channels.

Both events auto-register via `GameplayEventSchema` base class; no manual OpenAPI wiring.

### OpenAPI + mobile types

Pre-commit hook regenerates `openapi/openapi.yaml` + `mobile/src/api/schema.d.ts`. Confirm the two events show up. Add short aliases to `mobile/src/types/gameplay.ts` if needed for mobile cycles 6/7.

## QA

Automated:
- `cd core && uv run ruff check . && uv run pyright`.
- `cd server && uv run ruff check . && uv run pyright && uv run pytest`. Add tests for:
  - Photo upload+queue (state stays asked, PhotoQueuedEvent on hider channel only).
  - Photo upload+submit (transitions to submitted, PhotoSubmittedEvent on both channels, review_deadline is submitted_at + 30s).
  - Null submit (is_null_answer=true, photo_object_key=null, PhotoSubmittedEvent, no queued event).
  - Replace: two sequential uploads with submit=false; DB has latest key, old key orphaned in S3.
  - Unqueue: clears state, emits unqueue signal.
  - State-sensitive fetch: hider in asked (200 bytes), seeker in asked (403), seeker in submitted (200), any player in answered (200), null-answer fetch (404).
  - Submission lock: second hider submit while status=submitted → 409.
  - Invalid content-type (text/plain) → 415.
  - Wrong question type (upload to a radar question's /photo route) → 422.
  - Not in asked state (upload after submit) → 409.

Manual smoke via docker compose:
1. Ask a photo question (cycle 3 path).
2. `curl -H '...' -F 'file=@tree.jpg' -F 'submit=false' POST .../photo` → 204. `awslocal s3 ls` shows the object. Hider SSE gets `PhotoQueuedEvent`. Seeker SSE silent.
3. `curl GET .../photo` as hider → 200 bytes match.
4. `curl GET .../photo` as seeker → 403.
5. `curl -F 'file=@building.jpg' -F 'submit=false' POST .../photo` → 204; DB row points to new key; old key still present in S3.
6. `curl -F 'file=@final.jpg' -F 'submit=true' POST .../photo` → 204; `PhotoSubmittedEvent` on both SSE channels with review_deadline; status=submitted.
7. Second hider: `curl -F 'file=... -F submit=true'` → 409.
8. `curl GET .../photo` as seeker → 200 bytes.
9. Replay: ask → queue → `curl -X DELETE .../photo` → 204; status still asked; DB key cleared. Hider SSE gets unqueue signal.
10. Replay: ask → `curl -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"null": true}' POST .../photo` → 204; PhotoSubmittedEvent with `is_null_answer=true`; `GET .../photo` → 404.

## Dependencies

- Cycle 1 (models).
- Cycle 2 (S3 config + client).
- Cycle 3 (ask flow — needed to produce `asked` photo questions to upload against).

## Out of scope

title: Photo questions: review + reconciler auto-resolve
description:
## Scope

Seeker accept/reject endpoints, reconciler queries for submit + review timeouts, worker tasks for auto-resolve, answered-event wiring with `exclusion=NULL` + `total_exclusion` carry-forward, push notification types, SSE snapshot fields for mid-submitted reconnect, and veto/randomize dispatch for photo questions.

Design refs: §6.3 (review), §6.4 (auto-accept / auto-submit), §6.5 (veto/randomize/abandon), §6.7 (PhotoRejectedEvent + answered wiring), §6.8 (push), §6.9 (snapshot + history).

### Accept endpoint

`POST /games/{game_id}/questions/{question_id}/accept` — seeker-in-game.

Place logic in `core/src/hideandseek_core/logic/photo.py` (from cycle 4) alongside `_submit_photo_question`.

```python
def accept_photo(question: Question, player: Player) -> None:
    params = question.photo_params
    assert params is not None
    assert question.status == QuestionStatus.submitted
    params.review_decision = PhotoReviewDecision.accepted
    params.reviewed_at = datetime.now(UTC)
    params.reviewed_by = player.id
    question.status = QuestionStatus.answered
    question.answered_at = params.reviewed_at
    question.answer = (
        'null' if params.is_null_answer else params.photo_object_key
    )
    question.exclusion = None
    # total_exclusion carries forward via the existing null-exclusion handler.
    apply_null_exclusion(question)
    _log_question_answered(question)
```

Emit existing `HiderQuestionAnsweredEvent` + `SeekerQuestionAnsweredEvent`. Clients detect `question_type == photo` to render the photo viewer instead of a map delta.

### Reject endpoint

`POST /games/{game_id}/questions/{question_id}/reject` — seeker-in-game.

```python
def reject_photo(question: Question, player: Player) -> None:
    params = question.photo_params
    assert params is not None
    assert question.status == QuestionStatus.submitted
    params.review_decision = PhotoReviewDecision.rejected
    params.reviewed_at = datetime.now(UTC)
    params.reviewed_by = player.id
    # Loop back: null the submission so another attempt can take over.
    params.photo_object_key = None
    params.is_null_answer = False
    params.submitted_at = None
    params.submitted_by = None
    question.status = QuestionStatus.asked
    question.answerable_at = datetime.now(UTC)  # reset submit timer
    logger.info(
        'photo_rejected',
        game_id=str(question.game_id),
        question_id=str(question.id),
        reviewed_by=str(player.id),
    )
```

Emit `PhotoRejectedEvent` on both channels. S3 object from the rejected submission is **not** deleted (orphaned, consistent with §10).

```python
class PhotoRejectedEvent(GameplayEventSchema):
    question_id: uuid.UUID
    sequence: int
    reviewed_by: uuid.UUID
    rejected_at: datetime
    new_submit_deadline: datetime
```

`new_submit_deadline = now + timedelta(minutes=effective_photo_submit_min(game))` — computed at emit.

### Action race

First seeker to accept/reject wins. The validator re-reads `question.status == submitted` inside the request's transaction boundary; second caller gets 409. No explicit advisory lock — rely on Postgres row-level transaction semantics.

### Reconciler overdue queries

Add two queries to the reconciler's overdue-polling module (wherever the existing hiding→seeking and question-timeout queries live).

**Overdue submit deadlines**:

```python
# Fetch photo questions in asked state whose submit window has elapsed.
# effective_photo_submit_min is computed in Python after the fetch
# (join game + game_map, then apply the three-level fallback).
query = (
    select(Question, Game, GameMap)
    .join(Game, Question.game_id == Game.id)
    .join(GameMap, Game.game_map_id == GameMap.id)
    .where(
        Question.question_type == QuestionType.photo,
        Question.status == QuestionStatus.asked,
    )
)
# Filter in Python for rows where answerable_at + effective window < now.
```

Enqueue `auto_resolve_photo_submit(question_id)` with task-id `photo_submit:{question_id}` (log-grep observability; no revocation).

**Overdue review deadlines**:

```python
query = (
    select(Question, PhotoQuestionParams, Game, GameMap)
    .join(PhotoQuestionParams, PhotoQuestionParams.question_id == Question.id)
    .join(Game, Question.game_id == Game.id)
    .join(GameMap, Game.game_map_id == GameMap.id)
    .where(
        Question.question_type == QuestionType.photo,
        Question.status == QuestionStatus.submitted,
    )
)
# Filter in Python: submitted_at + effective_photo_review_sec < now.
```

Enqueue `auto_accept_photo(question_id)` with task-id `photo_review:{question_id}`.

### Worker tasks

`worker/src/hideandseek_worker/tasks/game_timers.py` (or an adjacent photo-specific module):

```python
@celery_app.task(name='auto_resolve_photo_submit')
def auto_resolve_photo_submit(question_id: str) -> None:
    with session_scope() as session:
        question = session.get(Question, UUID(question_id))
        if question is None or question.status != QuestionStatus.asked:
            return  # idempotency: state changed since overdue query
        params = question.photo_params
        assert params is not None
        if params.photo_object_key is not None or params.is_null_answer:
            # auto-submit queued answer
            params.submitted_at = datetime.now(UTC)
            params.submitted_by = None  # NULL sentinel for auto
            question.status = QuestionStatus.submitted
            # emit PhotoSubmittedEvent (both channels) with submitted_by=None
        else:
            question.status = QuestionStatus.abandoned
            # emit existing QuestionAbandonedEvent (both channels)

@celery_app.task(name='auto_accept_photo')
def auto_accept_photo(question_id: str) -> None:
    with session_scope() as session:
        question = session.get(Question, UUID(question_id))
        if question is None or question.status != QuestionStatus.submitted:
            return  # idempotency
        params = question.photo_params
        assert params is not None
        params.review_decision = PhotoReviewDecision.auto_accepted
        params.reviewed_at = datetime.now(UTC)
        params.reviewed_by = None  # NULL sentinel for auto
        question.status = QuestionStatus.answered
        question.answered_at = params.reviewed_at
        question.answer = 'null' if params.is_null_answer else params.photo_object_key
        question.exclusion = None
        apply_null_exclusion(question)
        # emit HiderQuestionAnsweredEvent + SeekerQuestionAnsweredEvent
```

### Veto + randomize

- **Veto**: existing `POST /questions/{id}/veto`. Confirm the allowed-state set includes `submitted` (design §6.5 — veto works in `{asked, submitted}`). If current logic only allows `asked`, extend.
- **Randomize**: `randomize_question()` in `logic/ask.py` dispatches per-type. Add:
  ```python
  case QuestionType.photo:
      slot = _pick_random_photo_slot(game, exclude_slot_index=question.slot_index)
      return ask_photo(game, player, seeker_location, slot)
  ```
  `_pick_random_photo_slot` picks a random available photo slot, excluding the current one so randomize actually changes subject.

### Push notifications

New `PushEventType` values:
- `photo_submitted` — to seekers when a hider submits.
- `photo_rejected` — to hiders when a seeker rejects.

Reuse existing event types for:
- Accept → `question_answered`.
- Submit-timeout (abandoned) → `question_abandoned`.
- Auto-accept → `question_answered`.

### SSE snapshot (server response schemas)

`HiderActiveQuestion` / `SeekerActiveQuestion` gain optional fields populated only for photo questions in `submitted` state:

```python
submitted_at: datetime | None = None
is_null_answer: bool | None = None
review_deadline: datetime | None = None
```

Lets a client reconnecting mid-review reconstruct the review banner without a separate GET.

`question_history` entries for photo questions: `parameters: PhotoEventParams`, `answer: str | None` (object key or `'null'`), `status: QuestionStatus`.

## QA

Automated:
- All packages: ruff + pyright clean.
- `cd server && uv run pytest`. Add tests for:
  - Accept: state transitions, exclusion=NULL, total_exclusion carried forward from prior question, events emitted, push sent.
  - Reject: loops to asked, nulls submission fields, resets answerable_at, PhotoRejectedEvent on both channels.
  - Accept race: two seekers call accept simultaneously; first wins with 200; second gets 409.
  - Reject-then-resubmit round-trip: status sequence `asked → submitted → asked → submitted → answered`.
  - `auto_resolve_photo_submit` idempotency: call twice → second is no-op.
  - `auto_resolve_photo_submit` with queued photo → auto-submit.
  - `auto_resolve_photo_submit` with nothing queued → abandoned.
  - `auto_accept_photo` idempotency + happy path → answered with auto_accepted decision.
  - SSE reconnect: snapshot for a submitted photo question carries `submitted_at`, `is_null_answer`, `review_deadline`.
  - Veto in `submitted` state → terminal vetoed.
  - Randomize → new photo question with different subject; original is terminal.
  - Push: `photo_submitted` envelope fires for seekers on submit; `photo_rejected` for hiders on reject.

Manual smoke via docker compose (full E2E via curl):
1. Ask → queue → submit → `POST accept` as seeker → both SSE channels emit AnsweredEvents. Question.answer = object_key. exclusion=NULL. total_exclusion matches prior question's total_exclusion. question_history entry present.
2. Ask → submit → `POST reject` → PhotoRejectedEvent on both; status back to asked; answerable_at advanced.
3. Shorten submit timer for dev (or directly UPDATE Game.photo_submit_min = 1) → ask → queue → wait → reconciler fires `auto_resolve_photo_submit` → PhotoSubmittedEvent with submitted_by=None; status=submitted.
4. Same shortened setup → ask → (no queue, no null) → wait → QuestionAbandonedEvent; status=abandoned.
5. Ask → submit → wait 30s → `auto_accept_photo` → AnsweredEvents; review_decision=auto_accepted; reviewed_by=NULL.
6. Veto in submitted state → vetoed terminal.
7. Randomize a photo question mid-asked → new photo question asked; different subject; original consumed.
8. Kill + restart server mid-submitted → reconnect SSE → snapshot active-question carries review_deadline → client can rebuild banner.
9. Push: tail `docker compose logs worker` + inspect SNS/LocalStack to confirm the right PushEventType fires on submit / reject.

## Dependencies

- Cycle 4 (submit + fetch; review logic builds on `submitted` state).

## Out of scope

- Mobile (cycles 6/7).

title: Photo questions: mobile seeker experience
description:
## Scope

Seeker-side mobile UI: belt picker, banner (asked/submitted), photo viewer modal, event wiring, question-history row.

Design refs: §7.0–§7.5, §9.1.

Hider UI is cycle 7 (separate bead, no hard ordering between 6 and 7 — pick whichever is easier to QA first).

### Palette (`mobile/src/theme/questionColors.ts` or wherever per-QuestionType colors are registered)

Add:
```ts
photo: {
  normal: 'rgb(156, 190, 208)',
  dimmed: 'rgb(199, 216, 225)',
}
```

### Icon

Camera icon — use `@expo/vector-icons` (`MaterialIcons` `camera-alt` or `Ionicons` `camera` — match the existing per-type icon library choice). Register alongside the existing per-type icon map.

### Subject label map

Client-side `PhotoSubject -> string` dictionary (labels per design §2 table), placed in `mobile/src/utils/photoSubjects.ts` (or similar):

```ts
export const PHOTO_SUBJECT_LABELS: Record<PhotoSubject, string> = {
  tree: 'A Tree',
  sky: 'The Sky',
  selfie: 'A Selfie',
  // ... full list from design §2
};
```

Labels live client-side per design §2 — the wire never carries them.

### Belt takeover — type selection

Add a sixth button to the belt takeover's type selection:
| Button | Icon | Label |
|--------|------|-------|
| Photo | `camera` | Photo |

Visible whenever the game has photo inventory (effectively always — only `Game.size == special` excludes it, and special is not user-selectable).

### Subject picker

On tap of the Photo button, show a scrollable list of subject slots from the inventory:
- Subject label (from `PHOTO_SUBJECT_LABELS`).
- `ask_count` pill if > 0 (e.g., "x2").
- Filter slots to `question_type === 'photo'` with `photo_subject` non-null.

No map preview — photo questions have no spatial overlay.

Tap a subject → the banner slides up with "Ask photo: [subject]?" + confirm/cancel.

### Ask call

On confirm: `POST /games/{id}/questions/photo` with `{slot_index}`. Belt closes; banner stays visible in asked state driven by SSE.

### Active question banner — `asked` state

- Icon (camera, photo palette color) + "Photo: [subject]".
- Status: "Waiting for hider to submit..."
- Countdown: submit deadline = `answerable_at + photo_submit_min` (client can compute from game state; server can also expose a derived field if easier).
- Abandon button (existing seeker-abandon flow — no new wiring).

### Active question banner — `submitted` state

Triggered by `PhotoSubmittedEvent`:
- Icon + "Photo: [subject]".
- Thumbnail: lazy-load from `GET /games/{id}/questions/{qid}/photo`. Spinner while loading. If `is_null_answer=true`: placeholder card "Null answer — hider reports nothing to photograph."
- Accept button (primary, photo palette color).
- Reject button (destructive-tinted) with confirm modal: "Reject this photo? The hider will have to resubmit."
- Review countdown from `review_deadline` in the event.

Accept call: `POST /games/{id}/questions/{qid}/accept`.
Reject call: `POST /games/{id}/questions/{qid}/reject`.

Both return 204 + emit SSE events; UI transitions follow from the events, not the REST response.

### Photo viewer modal

Full-screen viewer, triggered by tapping the thumbnail (in banner or history):
- Full-resolution image from `GET /photo` (HTTP cache handles subsequent loads; `Cache-Control: private, max-age=3600`).
- Pinch-to-zoom — try `react-native-gesture-handler` + `react-native-reanimated` first; add `react-native-image-zoom-viewer` only if native gesture feels wrong.
- Subject label + submitter name (resolve from roster in game state) + timestamp.
- Dismiss on tap anywhere / swipe down.

### Event handling (`mobile/src/state/gameplay.ts` or wherever SSE events land in the Zustand store)

- `QuestionAskedEvent` with `PhotoEventParams` → render asked banner, start submit countdown.
- `PhotoSubmittedEvent` → transition banner to submitted state, kick off thumbnail fetch, start review countdown from event.review_deadline.
- `PhotoRejectedEvent` → return to asked banner, reset submit countdown from event.new_submit_deadline, toast "Photo rejected — hider will resubmit."
- `SeekerQuestionAnsweredEvent` with `question_type=photo` → banner slides down, no map delta, add history row. Toast: "Photo accepted."
- `QuestionAbandonedEvent` for photo → banner slides down, toast "Photo question abandoned — hider didn't submit."

### Question history row (§9.1)

Photo variant:
- Subject label + thumbnail (or "null answer" placeholder, or "abandoned" chip if terminal state is abandoned).
- Review decision badge (accepted / rejected / auto-accepted / abandoned).
- No exclusion delta indicator.
- Tap → open photo viewer modal (unless null/abandoned, in which case tap is a no-op).

**Coordination with HideAndSeek-qpr**: if qpr has landed a shared `QuestionHistoryRow` component by the time this cycle starts, extend it with a photo variant. If qpr is still open, ship a minimal photo-only row here and revisit when qpr's shared component lands. Add a note to qpr to include photo semantics in its shared-row scope.

### SSE reconnect

When the game state snapshot arrives mid-submitted, the active-question shape should include `submitted_at`, `is_null_answer`, `review_deadline` (per cycle 5's snapshot fields). Wire the store to rehydrate the submitted banner from these fields on initial load.

### Seeker scrubber (HideAndSeek-0r6)

Out of scope here — 0r6 is a separate bead. Flag that the scrubber's current-question card for a photo row should show the photo + subject with no exclusion overlay on the scrubber map when 0r6 lands.

## QA

Automated:
- `cd mobile && npx tsc --noEmit && npx expo lint`.

Manual (user-driven on iOS sim — listed per design §7 + user-owns-mobile-QA memory):
- Ask each subject available at medium map size.
- Confirm banner transitions: asked → submitted → answered.
- Thumbnail loads on PhotoSubmittedEvent; spinner appears while loading.
- Null-answer placeholder renders when `is_null_answer=true`.
- Accept flow: tap Accept → banner slides down → toast → history row appears.
- Reject flow: tap Reject → confirm modal → confirm → banner returns to asked → toast.
- Auto-accept visible on review timeout (30s default) without any seeker action.
- Submit-timeout visible as abandoned banner dismissal (hider didn't submit).
- Rejection toast + re-transition to asked banner.
- Photo viewer modal: pinch-to-zoom smooth, submitter name resolves, timestamp readable, dismiss gesture works.
- Question history row: photo thumbnail visible, tap opens viewer.
- SSE disconnect + reconnect during submitted state: banner rehydrates with correct review_deadline and thumbnail.

## Dependencies

- Cycle 5 (server endpoints + events + snapshot fields + push).
- Soft coupling: HideAndSeek-qpr (question history row). Not a hard blocker.

## Out of scope

- Hider UI (cycle 7).
- Seeker scrubber integration (HideAndSeek-0r6).
- In-app camera (design §10 forbids).

title: Photo questions: mobile hider experience
description:
## Scope

Hider-side mobile UI using expo-image-picker: asked banner, picker flow, queued banner driven by `PhotoQueuedEvent`, submitted banner, reject/accept handling, null answer, 409 resilience.

Design refs: §8.1–§8.7.

No hard ordering vs. cycle 6 — pick whichever is easier to QA first or do them in parallel.

### Dependency

`expo-image-picker` — install via:
```bash
cd mobile && npx expo install expo-image-picker
```

Permission strings:
- iOS (`app.json` / `app.config.js` → `ios.infoPlist`): `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription` = "HideAndSeek needs access to your photo library so you can submit photos as evidence during the game."
- Android: expo-image-picker handles runtime permission request automatically; no manifest change beyond the Expo plugin.

### Active question banner — `asked` state, no queued photo

Triggered by `QuestionAskedEvent` with `PhotoEventParams`:
- Icon (camera, photo palette) + "Photo request: [subject]" — subject label from `PHOTO_SUBJECT_LABELS` (shared with cycle 6).
- Submit countdown from `answerable_at + photo_submit_min`.
- **Pick Photo** button (primary): `ImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAsync({ mediaTypes: ['images'], quality: 1 })`.
- **Null Answer** button (secondary) with confirm modal: "Submit null? Seekers will be told you can't photograph this."
- **Power-up** button (veto / randomize — existing flow).

### Photo picker flow

1. Tap Pick Photo → system picker opens.
2. User selects an image → app shows a preview card inside the banner:
   - Thumbnail (local URI from picker result).
   - **Submit Now** — immediate upload + submit.
   - **Queue** — upload with `submit=false`.
   - **Replace** — re-open picker.
   - **Cancel** — discard local selection; no upload.
3. **Upload happens on commit (Submit Now or Queue), not on initial selection.** Avoids uploading abandoned picks.

### Upload wire format

`POST /games/{id}/questions/{qid}/photo` as multipart:

```ts
const formData = new FormData();
formData.append('file', { uri, name: 'photo.jpg', type: 'image/jpeg' } as any);
formData.append('submit', submitNow ? 'true' : 'false');
await api.POST(...);
```

For null answer:
```ts
await api.POST(.../photo, { body: { null: true }, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } });
```

### Banner — `queued` state (driven by `PhotoQueuedEvent`)

**Critical**: this state is triggered by the server event, not local action. Every hider converges on the same view regardless of who uploaded. Local picker UI can optimistically show a spinner between commit and the event round-trip.

- Thumbnail from `GET /games/{id}/questions/{qid}/photo` (hiders can fetch in asked state).
- "Queued by [hider name] — will auto-submit at [deadline time]" (resolve name from roster; format deadline in local time).
- **Submit Now** — fires submit without re-upload.  
  **Open decision, flag during implementation**: server endpoint shape for "submit the already-queued photo." Options:
  - (a) Re-POST with `submit=true` and *no file*. Cleanest client-side; requires server-side handling for "multipart with no file but submit=true — use existing key." Update design doc §5.3 + §8.3 when picking this.
  - (b) Dedicated `POST /photo/submit` route. More explicit but adds a route.
  
  Default to (a) — fewest moving parts. Confirm with user before implementing.
- **Replace** — re-open picker; on commit, POST with `submit=false` and new file. Resulting `PhotoQueuedEvent` fans out.
- **Unqueue** — `DELETE /photo` (cycle 4 endpoint); returns to the pre-pick state.
- **Null** + **Power-up** buttons remain available.

### Banner — `submitted` state

Triggered by `PhotoSubmittedEvent` (applies to all hiders via submission lock):
- "Submitted — waiting for seeker review..."
- Review countdown from `review_deadline` in the event.
- No actions (picker disabled).

### Banner — rejected (`PhotoRejectedEvent`)

- Returns to asked state with a fresh picker flow.
- Toast: "Seeker rejected your photo — try again."

### Banner — accepted (`HiderQuestionAnsweredEvent` for photo)

- Banner slides down.
- Toast: "Seeker accepted your photo."

### Multi-hider race + 409 handling

If a hider is mid-pick when another hider submits:
- PhotoSubmittedEvent arrives → banner snaps to submitted state → picker modal auto-dismisses.
- Next tap on a Submit/Queue button from a stale picker returns 409.
- On 409: rehydrate banner from current server state (SSE snapshot or a fetch on the question). Show toast "Another hider already submitted."

Generalize 409 handling on the photo endpoint: any 409 → rehydrate from server state + toast. Covers the race above plus edge cases (submit after seeker just rejected and another hider re-queued).

### Permission handling

First time Pick Photo is tapped in a session:
- `ImagePicker.requestMediaLibraryPermissionsAsync()`.
- If denied: show a clear error banner with a link to Settings: "HideAndSeek needs photo library access to submit photos. Enable it in Settings → HideAndSeek."
- If denied and user retries: re-prompt only if permission is "undetermined" — else send them to Settings.

## QA

Automated:
- `cd mobile && npx tsc --noEmit && npx expo lint`.

Manual (user-driven, **physical device required** — photo picker + camera roll don't work well in sims):
- Asked banner appears on QuestionAskedEvent; subject label correct; countdown ticks.
- Pick Photo → select image → preview card appears inline.
- Submit Now: uploads + submits; banner transitions to submitted with review countdown.
- Queue: uploads + stays asked; banner transitions to queued state with thumbnail and "Queued by {me} — auto-submit at {deadline}."
- Replace while queued: re-pick, new upload, new thumbnail.
- Unqueue: clears local + server state; returns to asked.
- Null answer: confirm modal → submits null → banner transitions to submitted with no thumbnail.
- Auto-submit at deadline: queue, then wait (or shorten timer) → banner transitions to submitted automatically with `submitted_by=null`.
- Reject flow: banner returns to asked; toast shown.
- Accept flow: banner slides down; toast shown.
- Two-hider race (requires a second device/sim): both hiders are mid-pick; first to hit Submit wins; second's banner snaps to submitted state on PhotoSubmittedEvent; next tap on the second device returns 409 and rehydrates gracefully.
- Revoke photo-library permission in Settings → re-enter flow → permission prompt + graceful denial handling.
- SSE disconnect + reconnect mid-submitted → banner rehydrates with correct review_deadline.

## Dependencies

- Cycle 5 (server endpoints + events + snapshot fields + push).
- Coordination with cycle 6 (shared palette entry, subject label map, icon registration — whichever cycle lands first owns it, the other imports).

## Out of scope

- Seeker UI (cycle 6).
- In-app camera (design §10 explicitly forbids).
- Client-side image transform (resize/re-encode/EXIF strip) — design §10 defers.

QA'd against simulator with curl-driven 2nd hider + seeker. Banner layout polish tracked separately as HideAndSeek-mur.

title: Photo questions: expose submit/review timing overrides at game creation
description:
The Game model has photo_submit_min and photo_review_sec as nullable overrides (three-level fallback: request → map → code default), and GameMap has default_photo_submit_min / default_photo_review_sec. But none of these are reachable through the create-game flow:

Useful for playtest tuning — the curl walkthrough in server/CLAUDE.md already mentions setting photo_submit_min=2 via a direct UPDATE for fast manual QA. This bead lifts that capability into the supported create-game path.

Touches:
- core or server: nothing logic-wise; effective_photo_submit_min(game) / effective_photo_review_sec(game) already do the fallback.
- server: CreateGameRequest fields + create-game persistence + MapSummary defaults + OpenAPI regen.

title: Bug: utility belt taps dead after opening + dismissing seeker question history modal
description:
Repro (iOS sim, mid-game seeking phase, photo questions enabled):
1. Tap History on the seeker utility belt → SeekerQuestionHistoryModal opens.
2. Dismiss it (close button or swipe-down).
3. All subsequent taps on the utility belt are unresponsive. Map taps still work; only the belt UI is dead.

Workaround: reload Metro (`r`).

Suspected causes (in order of likelihood):
1. SeekerQuestionHistoryModal's scrubber uses a greedy PanResponder (`onStartShouldSetPanResponder: () => true`). If the modal unmounts mid-gesture or React Native's responder cleanup misses on iOS, the responder system may stay assigned to a now-dead view, swallowing all subsequent touches in the parent. Try moving the responder onto the inner track only with stricter `onStart/MoveShouldSetPanResponderCapture` semantics, or cancel the gesture explicitly on modal hide.
2. Stale Modal stacking. PhotoViewerModal at the gameplay screen root + SeekerQuestionHistoryModal + a tapped thumbnail opens PhotoViewerModal — three iOS Modals stacked. RN's Modal component on iOS pageSheet has known quirks where rapid stack/unstack can leave a phantom overlay.
